If this service is disabled, any MSDTC transaction interacting with a Kernel Resource Manager will fail and any services that explicitly depend on it will fail to start.

services.name: LanmanServer
services.description: Supports file, print, and named-pipe sharing over the network for this computer. If this service is stopped, these functions will be unavailable. If this service is disabled, any services that explicitly depend on it will fail to start.

services.name: LanmanWorkstation
services.description: Creates and maintains client network connections to remote servers using the SMB protocol. If this service is stopped, these connections will be unavailable. If this service is disabled, any services that explicitly depend on it will fail to start.

services.name: lfsvc
services.description: This service monitors the current location of the system and manages geofences (a geographical location with associated events).  If you turn off this service, applications will be unable to use or receive notifications for geolocation or geofences.

services.name: LicenseManager
services.description: Provides infrastructure support for the Microsoft Store.  This service is started on demand and if disabled then content acquired through the Microsoft Store will not function properly.

services.name: lltdsvc
services.description: Creates a Network Map, consisting of PC and device topology (connectivity) information, and metadata describing each PC and device.  If this service is disabled, the Network Map will not function properly.

services.name: lmhosts
services.description: Provides support for the NetBIOS over TCP/IP (NetBT) service and NetBIOS name resolution for clients on the network, therefore enabling users to share files, print, and log on to the network. If this service is stopped, these functions might be unavailable. If this service is disabled, any services that explicitly depend on it will fail to start.

services.name: LxpSvc
services.description: Provides infrastructure support for deploying and configuring localized Windows resources. This service is started on demand and, if disabled, additional Windows languages will not be deployed to the system, and Windows may not function properly.

services.name: MapsBroker
services.description: Windows service for application access to downloaded maps. This service is started on-demand by application accessing downloaded maps. Disabling this service will prevent apps from accessing maps.

services.name: MixedRealityOpenXRSvc
services.description: Enables Mixed Reality OpenXR runtime functionality

services.name: MSiSCSI
services.description: Manages Internet SCSI (iSCSI) sessions from this computer to remote iSCSI target devices. If this service is stopped, this computer will not be able to login or access iSCSI targets. If this service is disabled, any services that explicitly depend on it will fail to start.

services.name: msiserver
services.description: Adds, modifies, and removes applications provided as a Windows Installer (*.msi, *.msp) package. If this service is disabled, any services that explicitly depend on it will fail to start.

services.name: NaturalAuthentication
services.description: Signal aggregator service, that evaluates signals based on time, network, geolocation, bluetooth and cdf factors. Supported features are Device Unlock, Dynamic Lock and Dynamo MDM policies

services.name: NcaSvc
services.description: Provides DirectAccess status notification for UI components

services.name: NcbService
services.description: Brokers connections that allow Windows Store Apps to receive notifications from the internet.

services.name: NcdAutoSetup
services.description: Network Connected Devices Auto-Setup service monitors and installs qualified devices that connect to a qualified network. Stopping or disabling this service will prevent Windows from discovering and installing qualified network connected devices automatically. Users can still manually add network connected devices to a PC through the user interface.

services.name: Netlogon
services.description: Maintains a secure channel between this computer and the domain controller for authenticating users and services. If this service is stopped, the computer may not authenticate users and services and the domain controller cannot register DNS records. If this service is disabled, any services that explicitly depend on it will fail to start.

services.name: Netman
services.description: Manages objects in the Network and Dial-Up Connections folder, in which you can view both local area network and remote connections.

services.name: netprofm
services.description: Identifies the networks to which the computer has connected, collects and stores properties for these networks, and notifies applications when these properties change.

services.name: NetSetupSvc
services.description: The Network Setup Service manages the installation of network drivers and permits the configuration of low-level network settings.  If this service is stopped, any driver installations that are in-progress may be cancelled.

services.name: NetTcpPortSharing
services.description: Provides ability to share TCP ports over the net.tcp protocol.

services.name: NlaSvc
services.description: Collects and stores configuration information for the network and notifies programs when this information is modified. If this service is stopped, configuration information might be unavailable. If this service is disabled, any services that explicitly depend on it will fail to start.

services.name: nsi
services.description: This service delivers network notifications (e.g. interface addition/deleting etc) to user mode clients. Stopping this service will cause loss of network connectivity. If this service is disabled, any other services that explicitly depend on this service will fail to start.

services.name: ose64
services.description: Saves installation files used for updates and repairs and is required for the downloading of Setup updates and Watson error reports.

services.name: p2pimsvc
services.description: Provides identity services for the Peer Name Resolution Protocol (PNRP) and Peer-to-Peer Grouping services.  If disabled, the Peer Name Resolution Protocol (PNRP) and Peer-to-Peer Grouping services may not function, and some applications, such as HomeGroup and Remote Assistance, may not function correctly.

services.name: p2psvc
services.description: Enables multi-party communication using Peer-to-Peer Grouping.  If disabled, some applications, such as HomeGroup, may not function.

services.name: PcaSvc
services.description: This service provides support for the Program Compatibility Assistant (PCA).  PCA monitors programs installed and run by the user and detects known compatibility problems. If this service is stopped, PCA will not function properly.

services.name: PeerDistSvc
services.description: This service caches network content from peers on the local subnet.

services.name: perceptionsimulation
services.description: Enables spatial perception simulation, virtual camera management and spatial input simulation.

services.name: PerfHost
services.description: Enables remote users and 64-bit processes to query performance counters provided by 32-bit DLLs. If this service is stopped, only local users and 32-bit processes will be able to query performance counters provided by 32-bit DLLs.

services.name: PhoneSvc
services.description: Manages the telephony state on the device

services.name: pla
services.description: Performance Logs and Alerts Collects performance data from local or remote computers based on preconfigured schedule parameters, then writes the data to a log or triggers an alert. If this service is stopped, performance information will not be collected. If this service is disabled, any services that explicitly depend on it will fail to start.

services.name: PlugPlay
services.description: Enables a computer to recognize and adapt to hardware changes with little or no user input. Stopping or disabling this service will result in system instability.

services.name: PNRPAutoReg
services.description: This service publishes a machine name using the Peer Name Resolution Protocol.  Configuration is managed via the netsh context 'p2p pnrp peer'

services.name: PNRPsvc
services.description: Enables serverless peer name resolution over the Internet using the Peer Name Resolution Protocol (PNRP). If disabled, some peer-to-peer and collaborative applications, such as Remote Assistance, may not function.

services.name: PolicyAgent
services.description: Internet Protocol security (IPsec) supports network-level peer authentication, data origin authentication, data integrity, data confidentiality (encryption), and replay protection.  This service enforces IPsec policies created through the IP Security Policies snap-in or the command-line tool "netsh ipsec".  If you stop this service, you may experience network connectivity issues if your policy requires that connections use IPsec.  Also,remote management of Windows Defender Firewall is not available when this service is stopped.

services.name: Power
services.description: Manages power policy and power policy notification delivery.

services.name: PrintNotify
services.description: This service opens custom printer dialog boxes and handles notifications from a remote print server or a printer. If you turn off this service, you won’t be able to see printer extensions or notifications.

services.name: ProfSvc
services.description: This service is responsible for loading and unloading user profiles. If this service is stopped or disabled, users will no longer be able to successfully sign in or sign out, apps might have problems getting to users' data, and components registered to receive profile event notifications won't receive them.

services.name: PushToInstall
services.description: Provides infrastructure support for the Microsoft Store.  This service is started automatically and if disabled then remote installations will not function properly.

services.name: QWAVE
services.description: Quality Windows Audio Video Experience (qWave) is a networking platform for Audio Video (AV) streaming applications on IP home networks. qWave enhances AV streaming performance and reliability by ensuring network quality-of-service (QoS) for AV applications. It provides mechanisms for admission control, run time monitoring and enforcement, application feedback, and traffic prioritization.

services.name: RasAuto
services.description: Creates a connection to a remote network whenever a program references a remote DNS or NetBIOS name or address.

services.name: RasMan
services.description: Manages dial-up and virtual private network (VPN) connections from this computer to the Internet or other remote networks. If this service is disabled, any services that explicitly depend on it will fail to start.

services.name: RemoteAccess
services.description: Offers routing services to businesses in local area and wide area network environments.

services.name: RemoteRegistry
services.description: Enables remote users to modify registry settings on this computer. If this service is stopped, the registry can be modified only by users on this computer. If this service is disabled, any services that explicitly depend on it will fail to start.

services.name: RetailDemo
services.description: The Retail Demo service controls device activity while the device is in retail demo mode.

services.name: RpcLocator
services.description: In Windows 2003 and earlier versions of Windows, the Remote Procedure Call (RPC) Locator service manages the RPC name service database. In Windows Vista and later versions of Windows, this service does not provide any functionality and is present for application compatibility.

services.name: RtkAudioUniversalService
services.description: Realtek Audio Universal Service

services.name: SamSs
services.description: The startup of this service signals other services that the Security Accounts Manager (SAM) is ready to accept requests.  Disabling this service will prevent other services in the system from being notified when the SAM is ready, which may in turn cause those services to fail to start correctly. This service should not be disabled.

services.name: SCardSvr
services.description: Manages access to smart cards read by this computer. If this service is stopped, this computer will be unable to read smart cards. If this service is disabled, any services that explicitly depend on it will fail to start.

services.name: ScDeviceEnum
services.description: Creates software device nodes for all smart card readers accessible to a given session. If this service is disabled, WinRT APIs will not be able to enumerate smart card readers.

services.name: Schedule
services.description: Enables a user to configure and schedule automated tasks on this computer. The service also hosts multiple Windows system-critical tasks. If this service is stopped or disabled, these tasks will not be run at their scheduled times. If this service is disabled, any services that explicitly depend on it will fail to start.

services.name: SCPolicySvc
services.description: Allows the system to be configured to lock the user desktop upon smart card removal.

services.name: SDRSVC
services.description: Provides Windows Backup and Restore capabilities.

services.name: seclogon
services.description: Enables starting processes under alternate credentials. If this service is stopped, this type of logon access will be unavailable. If this service is disabled, any services that explicitly depend on it will fail to start.

services.name: SEMgrSvc
services.description: Manages payments and Near Field Communication (NFC) based secure elements.

services.name: SENS

services.name: SensorDataService

services.name: SensorService
services.description: A service for sensors that manages different sensors' functionality. Manages Simple Device Orientation (SDO) and History for sensors. Loads the SDO sensor that reports device orientation changes.  If this service is stopped or disabled, the SDO sensor will not be loaded and so auto-rotation will not occur. History collection from Sensors will also be stopped.

services.name: SensrSvc
services.description: Monitors various sensors in order to expose data and adapt to system and user state.  If this service is stopped or disabled, the display brightness will not adapt to lighting conditions. Stopping this service may affect other system functionality and features as well.

services.name: SessionEnv
services.description: Remote Desktop Configuration service (RDCS) is responsible for all Remote Desktop Services and Remote Desktop related configuration and session maintenance activities that require SYSTEM context. These include per-session temporary folders, RD themes, and RD certificates.

services.name: SgrmBroker
services.description: Monitors and attests to the integrity of the Windows platform.

services.name: SharedAccess

services.name: SharedRealitySvc
services.description: This service is used for Spatial Perception scenarios

services.name: ShellHWDetection
services.description: Provides notifications for AutoPlay hardware events.

services.name: shpamsvc
services.description: Manages profiles and accounts on a SharedPC configured device

services.name: smphost
services.description: Host service for the Microsoft Storage Spaces management provider. If this service is stopped or disabled, Storage Spaces cannot be managed.

services.name: SNMPTRAP
services.description: Receives trap messages generated by local or remote Simple Network Management Protocol (SNMP) agents and forwards the messages to SNMP management programs running on this computer. If this service is stopped, SNMP-based programs on this computer will not receive SNMP trap messages. If this service is disabled, any services that explicitly depend on it will fail to start.

services.name: spectrum
services.description: Enables spatial perception, spatial input, and holographic rendering.

services.name: Spooler
services.description: This service spools print jobs and handles interaction with the printer.  If you turn off this service, you won’t be able to print or see your printers.

services.name: sppsvc
services.description: Enables the download, installation and enforcement of digital licenses for Windows and Windows applications. If the service is disabled, the operating system and licensed applications may run in a notification mode. It is strongly recommended that you not disable the Software Protection service.

services.name: SSDPSRV
services.description: Discovers networked devices and services that use the SSDP discovery protocol, such as UPnP devices. Also announces SSDP devices and services running on the local computer. services.name: ssh-agent
services.description: Agent to hold private keys used for public key authentication.

services.name: SstpSvc

services.name: StateRepository

services.name: stisvc
services.description: Provides image acquisition services for scanners and cameras

services.name: StorSvc
services.description: Provides enabling services for storage settings and external storage expansion

services.name: svsvc
services.description: Verifies potential file system corruptions.

services.name: swprv

services.name: SysMain
services.description: Maintains and improves system performance over time.

services.name: TabletInputService
services.description: Enables Touch Keyboard and Handwriting Panel pen and ink functionality
services.display_name: Touch Keyboard and Handwriting Panel Service

services.name: TapiSrv
services.description: Provides Telephony API (TAPI) support for programs that control telephony devices on the local computer and, through the LAN, on servers that are also running the service.

services.name: TermService
services.description: Allows users to connect interactively to a remote computer. Remote Desktop and Remote Desktop Session Host Server depend on this service.  To prevent remote use of this computer, clear the checkboxes on the Remote tab of the System properties control panel item.

services.name: Themes
services.description: Provides user experience theme management.

services.name: TieringEngineService
services.description: Optimizes the placement of data in storage tiers on all tiered storage spaces in the system.

services.name: TokenBroker
services.description: This service is used by Web Account Manager to provide single-sign-on to apps and services.

services.name: TrkWks
services.description: Maintains links between NTFS files within a computer or across computers in a network.

services.name: TroubleshootingSvc
services.description: Enables automatic mitigation for known problems by applying recommended troubleshooting. If stopped, your device will not get recommended troubleshooting for problems on your device.

services.name: TrustedInstaller
services.description: Enables installation, modification, and removal of Windows updates and optional components. If this service is disabled, install or uninstall of Windows updates might fail for this computer.

services.name: tzautoupdate
services.description: Automatically sets the system time zone.

services.name: UevAgentService
services.description: Provides support for application and OS settings roaming

services.name: UmRdpService
services.description: Allows the redirection of Printers/Drives/Ports for RDP connections
services.display_name: Remote Desktop Services UserMode Port Redirector

services.name: upnphost
services.description: Allows UPnP devices to be hosted on this computer. If this service is stopped, any hosted UPnP devices will stop functioning and no additional hosted devices can be added. If this service is disabled, any services that explicitly depend on it will fail to start.

services.name: UserManager
services.description: User Manager provides the runtime components required for multi-user interaction.  If this service is stopped, some applications may not operate correctly.

services.name: vmicguestinterface
services.description: Provides an interface for the Hyper-V host to interact with specific services running inside the virtual machine.

services.name: vmicheartbeat
services.description: Monitors the state of this virtual machine by reporting a heartbeat at regular intervals. This service helps you identify running virtual machines that have stopped responding.

services.name: vmickvpexchange
services.description: Provides a mechanism to exchange data between the virtual machine and the operating system running on the physical computer.

services.name: vmicrdv
services.description: Provides a platform for communication between the virtual machine and the operating system running on the physical computer.

services.name: vmicshutdown
services.description: Provides a mechanism to shut down the operating system of this virtual machine from the management interfaces on the physical computer.

services.name: vmictimesync
services.description: Synchronizes the system time of this virtual machine with the system time of the physical computer.

services.name: vmicvmsession
services.description: Provides a mechanism to manage virtual machine with PowerShell via VM session without a virtual network.

services.name: vmicvss
services.description: Coordinates the communications that are required to use Volume Shadow Copy Service to back up applications and data on this virtual machine from the operating system on the physical computer.

services.name: VSS
services.description: Manages and implements Volume Shadow Copies used for backup and other purposes. If this service is stopped, shadow copies will be unavailable for backup and the backup may fail. If this service is disabled, any services that explicitly depend on it will fail to start.

services.name: W32Time
services.description: Maintains date and time synchronization on all clients and servers in the network. If this service is stopped, date and time synchronization will be unavailable. If this service is disabled, any services that explicitly depend on it will fail to start.

services.name: WaaSMedicSvc
services.description: Enables remediation and protection of Windows Update components.

services.name: WalletService
services.description: Hosts objects used by clients of the wallet

services.name: WarpJITSvc

services.name: WbioSrvc
services.description: The Windows biometric service gives client applications the ability to capture, compare, manipulate, and store biometric data without gaining direct access to any biometric hardware or samples. The service is hosted in a privileged SVCHOST process.

services.name: Wcmsvc
services.description: Makes automatic connect/disconnect decisions based on the network connectivity options currently available to the PC and enables management of network connectivity based on Group Policy settings.

services.name: wcncsvc
services.description: WCNCSVC hosts the Windows Connect Now Configuration which is Microsoft's Implementation of Wireless Protected Setup (WPS) protocol. This is used to configure Wireless LAN settings for an Access Point (AP) or a Wireless Device. The service is started programmatically as needed.

services.name: WdiServiceHost
services.description: The Diagnostic Service Host is used by the Diagnostic Policy Service to host diagnostics that need to run in a Local Service context.  If this service is stopped, any diagnostics that depend on it will no longer function.

services.name: WdiSystemHost
services.description: The Diagnostic System Host is used by the Diagnostic Policy Service to host diagnostics that need to run in a Local System context.  If this service is stopped, any diagnostics that depend on it will no longer function.

services.name: WebClient
services.description: Enables Windows-based programs to create, access, and modify Internet-based files. If this service is stopped, these functions will not be available. If this service is disabled, any services that explicitly depend on it will fail to start.

services.name: Wecsvc
services.description: This service manages persistent subscriptions to events from remote sources that support WS-Management protocol. This includes Windows Vista event logs, hardware and IPMI-enabled event sources. The service stores forwarded events in a local Event Log. If this service is stopped or disabled event subscriptions cannot be created and forwarded events cannot be accepted.

services.description: Windows Encryption Provider Host Service brokers encryption related functionalities from 3rd Party Encryption Providers to processes that need to evaluate and apply EAS policies. Also allows logs to be generated for diagnostic and repair services. If this service is stopped, error reporting might not work correctly and results of diagnostic services and repairs might not be displayed.

services.name: WiaRpc

services.name: Winmgmt
services.description: Provides a common interface and object model to access management information about operating system, devices, applications and services. If this service is stopped, most Windows-based software will not function properly. If this service is disabled, any services that explicitly depend on it will fail to start.

services.name: WinRM
services.description: Windows Remote Management (WinRM) service implements the WS-Management protocol for remote management. WS-Management is a standard web services protocol used for remote software and hardware management. The WinRM service listens on the network for WS-Management requests and processes them. The WinRM Service needs to be configured with a listener using winrm.cmd command line tool or through Group Policy in order for it to listen over the network. The WinRM service provides access to WMI data and enables event collection. Event collection and subscription to events require that the service is running. WinRM messages use HTTP and HTTPS as transports. The WinRM service does not depend on IIS but is preconfigured to share a port with IIS on the same machine.  The WinRM service reserves the /wsman URL prefix. To prevent conflicts with IIS, administrators should ensure that any websites hosted on IIS do not use the /wsman URL prefix.

services.name: wisvc
services.description: Provides infrastructure support for the Windows Insider Program. This service must remain enabled for the Windows Insider Program to work.

services.name: WlanSvc
services.description: The WLANSVC service provides the logic required to configure, discover, connect to, and disconnect from a wireless local area network (WLAN) as defined by IEEE 802.11 standards. It also contains the logic to turn your computer into a software access point so that other devices or computers can connect to your computer wirelessly using a WLAN adapter that can support this. Stopping or disabling the WLANSVC service will make all WLAN adapters on your computer inaccessible from the Windows networking UI. It is strongly recommended that you have the WLANSVC service running if your computer has a WLAN adapter.

services.name: wlidsvc
services.description: Enables user sign-in through Microsoft account identity services. If this service is stopped, users will not be able to logon to the computer with their Microsoft account.

services.name: WpcMonSvc

services.description: Provides secure storage and retrieval of credentials to users, applications and security service packages.

services.name: vds
services.description: Provides management services for disks, volumes, file systems, and storage arrays.

services.name: vmicguestinterface
services.description: Provides an interface for the Hyper-V host to interact with specific services running inside the virtual machine.

services.name: vmicheartbeat
services.description: Monitors the state of this virtual machine by reporting a heartbeat at regular intervals. This service helps you identify running virtual machines that have stopped responding.

services.name: vmickvpexchange
services.description: Provides a mechanism to exchange data between the virtual machine and the operating system running on the physical computer.

services.name: vmicrdv
services.description: Provides a platform for communication between the virtual machine and the operating system running on the physical computer.

services.name: vmicshutdown
services.description: Provides a mechanism to shut down the operating system of this virtual machine from the management interfaces on the physical computer.

services.name: vmictimesync
services.description: Synchronizes the system time of this virtual machine with the system time of the physical computer.

services.name: vmicvmsession
services.description: Provides a mechanism to manage virtual machine with PowerShell via VM session without a virtual network.

services.name: vmicvss
services.description: Coordinates the communications that are required to use Volume Shadow Copy Service to back up applications and data on this virtual machine from the operating system on the physical computer.

services.name: VSS
services.description: Manages and implements Volume Shadow Copies used for backup and other purposes. If this service is stopped, shadow copies will be unavailable for backup and the backup may fail. If this service is disabled, any services that explicitly depend on it will fail to start.

services.name: W32Time
services.description: Maintains date and time synchronization on all clients and servers in the network. If this service is stopped, date and time synchronization will be unavailable. If this service is disabled, any services that explicitly depend on it will fail to start.

services.name: WaaSMedicSvc
services.description: Enables remediation and protection of Windows Update components.

services.name: WalletService
services.description: Hosts objects used by clients of the wallet

services.name: WarpJITSvc
services.description: Provides a JIT out of process service for WARP when running with ACG enabled.

services.name: wbengine
services.description: The WBENGINE service is used by Windows Backup to perform backup and recovery operations. If this service is stopped by a user, it may cause the currently running backup or recovery operation to fail. Disabling this service may disable backup and recovery operations using Windows Backup on this computer.

services.name: WbioSrvc
services.description: The Windows biometric service gives client applications the ability to capture, compare, manipulate, and store biometric data without gaining direct access to any biometric hardware or samples. The service is hosted in a privileged SVCHOST process.

services.name: Wcmsvc
services.description: Makes automatic connect/disconnect decisions based on the network connectivity options currently available to the PC and enables management of network connectivity based on Group Policy settings.

services.name: wcncsvc
services.description: WCNCSVC hosts the Windows Connect Now Configuration which is Microsoft's Implementation of Wireless Protected Setup (WPS) protocol. This is used to configure Wireless LAN settings for an Access Point (AP) or a Wireless Device. The service is started programmatically as needed.

services.name: WdiServiceHost
services.description: The Diagnostic Service Host is used by the Diagnostic Policy Service to host diagnostics that need to run in a Local Service context.  If this service is stopped, any diagnostics that depend on it will no longer function.

services.name: WdiSystemHost
services.description: The Diagnostic System Host is used by the Diagnostic Policy Service to host diagnostics that need to run in a Local System context.  If this service is stopped, any diagnostics that depend on it will no longer function.

services.name: WebClient
services.description: Enables Windows-based programs to create, access, and modify Internet-based files. If this service is stopped, these functions will not be available. If this service is disabled, any services that explicitly depend on it will fail to start.

services.name: Wecsvc
services.description: This service manages persistent subscriptions to events from remote sources that support WS-Management protocol. This includes Windows Vista event logs, hardware and IPMI-enabled event sources. The service stores forwarded events in a local Event Log. If this service is stopped or disabled event subscriptions cannot be created and forwarded events cannot be accepted.

services.name: WEPHOSTSVC
services.description: Windows Encryption Provider Host Service brokers encryption related functionalities from 3rd Party Encryption Providers to processes that need to evaluate and apply EAS policies. Stopping this will compromise EAS compliancy checks that have been established by the connected Mail Accounts

services.name: wercplsupport
services.description: This service provides support for viewing, sending and deletion of system-level problem reports for the Problem Reports control panel.

services.name: WerSvc
services.description: Allows errors to be reported when programs stop working or responding and allows existing solutions to be delivered. Also allows logs to be generated for diagnostic and repair services. If this service is stopped, error reporting might not work correctly and results of diagnostic services and repairs might not be displayed.

services.name: WFDSConMgrSvc
services.description: Manages connections to wireless services, including wireless display and docking.
services.display_name: Wi-Fi Direct Services Connection Manager Service

services.name: WiaRpc
services.description: Launches applications associated with still image acquisition events.

services.name: Winmgmt
services.description: Provides a common interface and object model to access management information about operating system, devices, applications and services. If this service is stopped, most Windows-based software will not function properly. If this service is disabled, any services that explicitly depend on it will fail to start.

services.name: WinRM
services.description: Windows Remote Management (WinRM) service implements the WS-Management protocol for remote management. WS-Management is a standard web services protocol used for remote software and hardware management. The WinRM service listens on the network for WS-Management requests and processes them. The WinRM Service needs to be configured with a listener using winrm.cmd command line tool or through Group Policy in order for it to listen over the network. The WinRM service provides access to WMI data and enables event collection. Event collection and subscription to events require that the service is running. WinRM messages use HTTP and HTTPS as transports. The WinRM service does not depend on IIS but is preconfigured to share a port with IIS on the same machine.  The WinRM service reserves the /wsman URL prefix. To prevent conflicts with IIS, administrators should ensure that any websites hosted on IIS do not use the /wsman URL prefix.

services.name: wisvc
services.description: Provides infrastructure support for the Windows Insider Program. This service must remain enabled for the Windows Insider Program to work.

services.name: WlanSvc
services.description: The WLANSVC service provides the logic required to configure, discover, connect to, and disconnect from a wireless local area network (WLAN) as defined by IEEE 802.11 standards. It also contains the logic to turn your computer into a software access point so that other devices or computers can connect to your computer wirelessly using a WLAN adapter that can support this. Stopping or disabling the WLANSVC service will make all WLAN adapters on your computer inaccessible from the Windows networking UI. It is strongly recommended that you have the WLANSVC service running if your computer has a WLAN adapter.

services.name: wlidsvc
services.description: Enables user sign-in through Microsoft account identity services. If this service is stopped, users will not be able to logon to the computer with their Microsoft account.

services.name: wlpasvc
services.description: This service provides profile management for subscriber identity modules

services.name: WManSvc
services.description: Performs management including Provisioning and Enrollment activities

services.name: wmiApSrv
services.description: Provides performance library information from Windows Management Instrumentation (WMI) providers to clients on the network. This service only runs when Performance Data Helper is activated.

services.name: WMPNetworkSvc
services.description: Shares Windows Media Player libraries to other networked players and media devices using Universal Plug and Play
services.display_name: Windows Media Player Network Sharing Service

services.name: workfolderssvc
services.description: This service syncs files with the Work Folders server, enabling you to use the files on any of the PCs and devices on which you've set up Work Folders.

services.name: WpcMonSvc
services.description: Enforces parental controls for child accounts in Windows. If this service is stopped or disabled, parental controls may not be enforced.

services.name: WPDBusEnum
services.description: Enforces group policy for removable mass-storage devices. Enables applications such as Windows Media Player and Image Import Wizard to transfer and synchronize content using removable mass-storage devices.

services.name: WpnService
services.description: This service runs in session 0 and hosts the notification platform and connection provider which handles the connection between the device and WNS server.

services.name: WSearch
services.description: Provides content indexing, property caching, and search results for files, e-mail, and other content.

services.name: wuauserv
services.description: Enables the detection, download, and installation of updates for Windows and other programs. If this service is disabled, users of this computer will not be able to use Windows Update or its automatic updating feature, and programs will not be able to use the Windows Update Agent (WUA) API.

services.name: WwanSvc
services.description: This service manages mobile broadband (GSM & CDMA) data card/embedded module adapters and connections by auto-configuring the networks. It is strongly recommended that this service be kept running for best user experience of mobile broadband devices.

services.name: XblAuthManager
services.description: Provides authentication and authorization services for interacting with Xbox Live. If this service is stopped, some applications may not operate correctly.

services.name: XblGameSave
services.description: This service syncs save data for Xbox Live save enabled games.  If this service is stopped, game save data will not upload to or download from Xbox Live.

services.name: XboxGipSvc

services.name: XboxNetApiSvc
services.description: This service supports the Windows.Networking.XboxLive application programming interface.

fields.name: Agent log tail
fields.description: Shows the last lines of the agent log: journald unit ulrmm-agent, else a log file under /opt/ulrmm-agent or /var/log, else syslog. Exit 3 when none exists.
fields.script_body:
#!/bin/sh
# Shows the last lines of the ULRMM agent log (journald unit, else log file under the agent directory or syslog).
# Variables: LINES (100, 1-2000)
# Exit: 0 log shown, 3 bad input or no agent log found
PATH=/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin
export PATH LC_ALL=C
set -u

N=${LINES:-100}
case $N in '' | *[!0-9]*) echo "LINES must be a whole number"; exit 3 ;; esac
{ [ "${#N}" -le 4 ] && [ "$N" -ge 1 ] && [ "$N" -le 2000 ]; } || { echo "LINES must be between 1 and 2000"; exit 3; }

if [ -d /run/systemd/system ] && command -v journalctl >/dev/null 2>&1 && systemctl cat ulrmm-agent >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "== journal, unit ulrmm-agent, last $N lines"
  journalctl -u ulrmm-agent -n "$N" --no-pager -q 2>/dev/null | cut -c1-400
  exit 0
fi
for f in /opt/ulrmm-agent/*.log /opt/ulrmm-agent/logs/*.log /var/log/ulrmm-agent.log /var/log/ulrmm-agent/*.log; do
  [ -f "$f" ] || continue
  echo "== $f, last $N lines"
  tail -n "$N" "$f" | cut -c1-400
  exit 0
done
for f in /var/log/messages /var/log/syslog; do
  [ -r "$f" ] || continue
  out=$(grep -i 'ulrmm-agent' "$f" | tail -n "$N")
  [ -n "$out" ] || continue
  echo "== $f, last $N agent lines"
  printf '%s\n' "$out" | cut -c1-400
  exit 0
done
echo "No agent log found: no journal unit ulrmm-agent, no log file under /opt/ulrmm-agent or /var/log, no syslog entries"
exit 3

fields.name: Agent services status
fields.description: Shows install, enable and run state of the agent and the MeshCentral agent (systemd or OpenRC) and the agent version. Exit 1 when the agent is not running.
fields.script_body:
#!/bin/sh
# Shows install, enable and run state of the ULRMM agent and the MeshCentral agent, plus the agent version.
# Variables: none
# Exit: 0 agent running, 1 agent installed but not running, 2 only the MeshCentral agent is stopped, 3 agent not installed or no service manager
PATH=/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin
export PATH LC_ALL=C
set -u

if [ -d /run/systemd/system ] && command -v systemctl >/dev/null 2>&1; then mgr=systemd
elif command -v rc-service >/dev/null 2>&1; then mgr=openrc
else echo "Unsupported: neither systemd nor OpenRC found"; exit 3; fi

# state <service> <binary>: prints "installed|enabled|running"
state() {
  inst=no en=no run=no
  [ -x "$2" ] && inst=yes
  if [ $mgr = systemd ]; then
    systemctl cat "$1" >/dev/null 2>&1 && inst=yes
    systemctl is-enabled "$1" >/dev/null 2>&1 && en=yes
    systemctl is-active "$1" >/dev/null 2>&1 && run=yes
  else
    [ -e "/etc/init.d/$1" ] && inst=yes
    rc-update show 2>/dev/null | grep -qw "^ *$1" && en=yes
    rc-service "$1" status >/dev/null 2>&1 && run=yes
  fi
  echo "$inst|$en|$run"
}
agent=/opt/ulrmm-agent/ulrmm-agent
mesh=/opt/ulrmm-mesh/meshagent
a=$(state ulrmm-agent "$agent")
m=$(state meshagent "$mesh")
case $a in no*) echo "ULRMM agent is not installed on this system"; echo "mesh agent: installed=${m%%|*}"; exit 3 ;; esac
ver=''
if [ -x "$agent" ]; then
  if command -v timeout >/dev/null 2>&1; then ver=$(timeout 10 "$agent" -version 2>&1 </dev/null | head -n 1)
  else ver=$("$agent" -version 2>&1 </dev/null | head -n 1); fi
fi
mtime=''
[ -f "$mesh" ] && mtime=$(date -r "$mesh" '+%Y-%m-%d' 2>/dev/null)
ai=${a%%|*}; r=${a#*|}; ae=${r%%|*}; ar=${r#*|}
mi=${m%%|*}; r=${m#*|}; me=${r%%|*}; mr=${r#*|}
rc=0
[ "$ar" = yes ] || rc=1
[ $rc -eq 0 ] && [ "$mi" = yes ] && [ "$mr" != yes ] && rc=2
case $rc in
0) echo "OK: agent running${mi:+, mesh agent installed=$mi running=$mr}" ;;
1) echo "ERROR: agent installed but not running" ;;
2) echo "WARNING: agent running, mesh agent not running" ;;
esac
echo "ulrmm-agent: installed=$ai enabled=$ae running=$ar version=${ver:-unknown} ($mgr)"
echo "meshagent:   installed=$mi enabled=$me running=$mr binary built ${mtime:-unknown}"
exit $rc

fields.name: ClamAV install
fields.description: Installs ClamAV and freshclam with the system package manager, enables automatic signature updates and loads the signatures.
fields.script_body:
#!/bin/sh
# Installs ClamAV with freshclam, enables automatic signature updates and loads the signatures.
# Variables: ENABLE_EPEL (true) add EPEL on RHEL-family systems when ClamAV is not available otherwise.
# Exit: 0 installed or already in place, 1 failed, 3 bad input or unsupported system.
PATH=/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin
export PATH
set -u

enable_epel=${ENABLE_EPEL:-true}
case "$enable_epel" in
true | false) ;;
*) echo "ENABLE_EPEL must be true or false"; exit 3 ;;
esac

[ "$(id -u)" -eq 0 ] || { echo "Must run as root"; exit 3; }

# Runs a package manager command quietly and shows its last lines only when it fails.
pkg() {
	out=$("$@" 2>&1)
	prc=$?
	[ $prc -eq 0 ] || echo "$out" | tail -n 5
	return $prc
}

if command -v clamscan >/dev/null 2>&1 && command -v freshclam >/dev/null 2>&1; then
	echo "ClamAV already installed: $(clamscan --version 2>/dev/null)"
else
	if command -v apt-get >/dev/null 2>&1; then
		export DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive
		pkg apt-get update -q && pkg apt-get install -y -q clamav clamav-freshclam
	elif command -v dnf >/dev/null 2>&1 || command -v yum >/dev/null 2>&1; then
		pm=dnf
		command -v dnf >/dev/null 2>&1 || pm=yum
		if ! "$pm" -q list clamav >/dev/null 2>&1; then
			if [ "$enable_epel" != true ]; then
				echo "ClamAV is not in the enabled repositories and ENABLE_EPEL is false"
				exit 3
			fi
			echo "Adding the EPEL repository"
			pkg "$pm" -y -q install epel-release || {
				echo "Cannot install epel-release (on RHEL enable codeready-builder and install EPEL from fedoraproject.org)"
				exit 1
			}
		fi
		pkg "$pm" -y -q install clamav clamav-update
	elif command -v zypper >/dev/null 2>&1; then
		pkg zypper --non-interactive --quiet install clamav
	elif command -v pacman >/dev/null 2>&1; then
		# No -y here: a refresh without a full upgrade is a partial upgrade on Arch.
		pkg pacman -S --noconfirm --needed clamav || { echo "If the package was not found, run pacman -Syu first"; false; }
	elif command -v apk >/dev/null 2>&1; then
		pkg apk add -q clamav clamav-scanner freshclam
	else
		echo "No supported package manager (apt-get, dnf, yum, zypper, pacman, apk)"
		exit 3
	fi
	rc=$?
	if [ $rc -ne 0 ] || ! command -v clamscan >/dev/null 2>&1 || ! command -v freshclam >/dev/null 2>&1; then
		echo "Package installation failed (exit $rc)"
		exit 1
	fi
	echo "Installed: $(clamscan --version 2>/dev/null)"
fi

# Some packages ship freshclam.conf with an "Example" line that disables it.
for conf in /etc/freshclam.conf /etc/clamav/freshclam.conf; do
	if [ -f "$conf" ] && grep -q '^Example' "$conf"; then
		sed -i 's/^Example/#Example/' "$conf"
		echo "Enabled $conf (commented out the Example line)"
	fi
done

unit=""
if [ -d /run/systemd/system ] && command -v systemctl >/dev/null 2>&1; then
	for u in clamav-freshclam.service freshclam.service freshclam.timer; do
		if systemctl cat "$u" >/dev/null 2>&1; then unit=$u; break; fi
	done
fi
openrc=false
if [ -z "$unit" ] && command -v rc-service >/dev/null 2>&1 && [ -e /etc/init.d/freshclam ]; then
	openrc=true
fi

# Load the signatures once in the foreground so the result is known now.
if [ -n "$unit" ]; then systemctl stop "$unit" >/dev/null 2>&1; fi
if $openrc; then rc-service freshclam stop >/dev/null 2>&1; fi
out=$(freshclam --stdout 2>&1)
frc=$?
case $frc in
0 | 1) echo "Signatures: $(echo "$out" | sed -n 's/.*\(daily\.c[lv]d.*\)/\1/p' | tail -n 1)" ;;
*)
	echo "freshclam failed (exit $frc):"
	echo "$out" | grep -iE 'error|warning' | tail -n 5
	;;
esac

if [ -n "$unit" ]; then
	if systemctl enable --now "$unit" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
		echo "Automatic updates: $unit enabled and running"
	else
		echo "Could not enable $unit"
		frc=1
	fi
elif $openrc; then
	rc-update add freshclam default >/dev/null 2>&1
	if rc-service freshclam start >/dev/null 2>&1; then
		echo "Automatic updates: OpenRC service freshclam enabled and running"
	else
		echo "Could not start the OpenRC service freshclam"
		frc=1
	fi
else
	echo "Automatic updates: no running systemd or OpenRC found, schedule the signature update script instead"
fi

case $frc in
0 | 1) exit 0 ;;
*) exit 1 ;;
esac

variables.name: ENABLE_EPEL
variables.label: Add EPEL on RHEL family

fields.name: ClamAV scan
fields.description: Scans the given paths with clamscan and lists infected files without changing them. Exit 1 on infection, 2 on scan errors.
fields.script_body:
#!/bin/sh
# Scans paths on demand with clamscan and prints a summary with the infected files. Changes nothing.
# Variables: PATHS (/home,/root,/tmp,/var/tmp) comma or newline separated, EXCLUDE ("") paths to skip,
#   MAX_FILESIZE_MB (100) larger files are skipped.
# Exit: 0 clean, 1 infection found, 2 scan finished with errors, 3 bad input or ClamAV missing.
PATH=/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin
export PATH
set -u

paths=${PATHS:-/home,/root,/tmp,/var/tmp}
exclude=${EXCLUDE:-}
max_mb=${MAX_FILESIZE_MB:-100}

case "$max_mb" in
'' | *[!0-9]*) echo "MAX_FILESIZE_MB must be a whole number"; exit 3 ;;
esac
[ "$max_mb" -ge 1 ] && [ "$max_mb" -le 4000 ] || { echo "MAX_FILESIZE_MB must be 1-4000"; exit 3; }

command -v clamscan >/dev/null 2>&1 || {
	echo "clamscan not found, run the ClamAV install script first (package clamav)"
	exit 3
}

nl='
'
# Build the argument list in "$@"; clamscan takes the exclusions as regular expressions.
set --
add_excl() {
	case "$1" in
	/*) ;;
	*) echo "Exclusion is not an absolute path: $1"; exit 3 ;;
	esac
	re=$(printf '%s' "${1%/}" | sed 's/[][\.*^$+?(){}|]/\\&/g')
	excl_args="$excl_args${nl}--exclude-dir=^$re(/|\$)${nl}--exclude=^$re\$"
}
excl_args=""
for p in /proc /sys /dev /run; do add_excl "$p"; done

old_ifs=$IFS
IFS=",$nl"
for p in $exclude; do
	p=$(printf '%s' "$p" | sed 's/^[[:space:]]*//; s/[[:space:]]*$//')
	[ -n "$p" ] && add_excl "$p"
done
targets=0
for p in $paths; do
	p=$(printf '%s' "$p" | sed 's/^[[:space:]]*//; s/[[:space:]]*$//')
	[ -n "$p" ] || continue
	case "$p" in
	/*) ;;
	*) echo "Path is not absolute: $p"; exit 3 ;;
	esac
	if [ -e "$p" ]; then
		set -- "$@" "$p"
		targets=$((targets + 1))
	else
		echo "Skipped, does not exist: $p"
	fi
done
IFS=$nl
for a in $excl_args; do set -- "$@" "$a"; done
IFS=$old_ifs

[ "$targets" -gt 0 ] || { echo "None of the paths exist: $paths"; exit 3; }

log=$(mktemp) || exit 1
trap 'rm -f "$log"' EXIT

# clamscan accepts at most 4000M for both limits.
scan_mb=$((max_mb * 4))
[ "$scan_mb" -gt 4000 ] && scan_mb=4000
prio=""
command -v nice >/dev/null 2>&1 && prio="nice -n 10"
# shellcheck disable=SC2086
$prio clamscan --recursive --infected --stdout --max-filesize="${max_mb}M" --max-scansize="${scan_mb}M" "$@" >"$log" 2>&1
rc=$?

infected=$(grep -c ' FOUND$' "$log")
scanned=$(sed -n 's/^Scanned files: //p' "$log")
errors=$(sed -n 's/^Total errors: //p' "$log")
case $rc in
0) echo "CLEAN: ${scanned:-0} files scanned, no infection found" ;;
1) echo "INFECTED: $infected file(s) found in ${scanned:-0} scanned files" ;;
*) echo "ERROR: clamscan exit $rc, ${errors:-unknown} error(s), ${scanned:-0} files scanned" ;;
esac
grep ' FOUND$' "$log" | head -n 50
[ "$infected" -gt 50 ] && echo "... $((infected - 50)) more"
if [ $rc -gt 1 ]; then
	grep -E '^(ERROR|WARNING|LibClamAV Error)' "$log" | sort | uniq | head -n 10
fi
sed -n -E '/^(Known viruses|Engine version|Data scanned|Time):/p' "$log"

case $rc in
0) exit 0 ;;
1) exit 1 ;;
*) exit 2 ;;
esac

variables.help: Absolute paths, comma or newline separated.
variables.name: PATHS
variables.label: Paths to scan

variables.help: Absolute paths, comma or newline separated. /proc, /sys, /dev and /run are always skipped.
variables.name: EXCLUDE
variables.label: Paths to skip

variables.help: Larger files are not scanned.
variables.name: MAX_FILESIZE_MB
variables.label: Skip files larger than (MB)

fields.name: ClamAV signature update
fields.description: Runs freshclam now, pausing the freshclam service for the run. Exit 1 when the update fails.
fields.script_body:
#!/bin/sh
# Updates the ClamAV signatures now with freshclam.
# Variables: none.
# Exit: 0 updated or already current, 1 update failed, 3 ClamAV is not installed.
PATH=/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin
export PATH
set -u

command -v freshclam >/dev/null 2>&1 || {
	echo "freshclam not found, run the ClamAV install script first (package clamav / clamav-update / freshclam)"
	exit 3
}

# A running freshclam daemon holds the log and database lock; pause it for the manual run.
unit=""
if [ -d /run/systemd/system ] && command -v systemctl >/dev/null 2>&1; then
	for u in clamav-freshclam.service freshclam.service; do
		if systemctl is-active --quiet "$u"; then unit=$u; break; fi
	done
fi
openrc=false
if [ -z "$unit" ] && command -v rc-service >/dev/null 2>&1 && rc-service freshclam status >/dev/null 2>&1; then
	openrc=true
fi
[ -n "$unit" ] && systemctl stop "$unit"
$openrc && rc-service freshclam stop >/dev/null 2>&1

out=$(freshclam --stdout 2>&1)
rc=$?

[ -n "$unit" ] && systemctl start "$unit"
$openrc && rc-service freshclam start >/dev/null 2>&1

case $rc in
0 | 1)
	if echo "$out" | grep -q 'c[lv]d updated'; then echo "Signatures updated"; else echo "Signatures already current"; fi
	echo "$out" | sed -n -E 's/.*((main|daily|bytecode)\.c[lv]d.*)/\1/p'
	exit 0
	;;
*)
	echo "Signature update failed (freshclam exit $rc)"
	echo "$out" | grep -iE 'error|warning' | tail -n 5
	exit 1
	;;
esac

fields.name: ClamAV status
fields.description: Checks that ClamAV is installed, how old the signatures are and whether automatic updates run.
fields.script_body:
#!/bin/sh
# Checks ClamAV: installed, signature age and whether automatic signature updates run.
# Variables: WARN_DAYS (2) and FAIL_DAYS (7) signature age thresholds in days.
# Exit: 0 ok, 1 not installed or signatures older than FAIL_DAYS, 2 warning, 3 bad input.
PATH=/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin
export PATH
set -u

warn_days=${WARN_DAYS:-2}
fail_days=${FAIL_DAYS:-7}
for v in "$warn_days" "$fail_days"; do
	case "$v" in
	'' | *[!0-9]*) echo "WARN_DAYS and FAIL_DAYS must be whole numbers"; exit 3 ;;
	esac
done
[ "$warn_days" -le "$fail_days" ] || { echo "WARN_DAYS must not be larger than FAIL_DAYS"; exit 3; }

if ! command -v clamscan >/dev/null 2>&1; then
	echo "FAIL: ClamAV is not installed"
	exit 1
fi
version=$(clamscan --version 2>/dev/null)

dbdir=""
for conf in /etc/clamav/freshclam.conf /etc/freshclam.conf; do
	[ -f "$conf" ] || continue
	dbdir=$(sed -n 's/^DatabaseDirectory[[:space:]]\{1,\}//p' "$conf" | tail -n 1)
	break
done
[ -n "$dbdir" ] || dbdir=/var/lib/clamav

newest=0
for f in "$dbdir"/daily.cld "$dbdir"/daily.cvd; do
	[ -f "$f" ] || continue
	t=$(stat -c %Y "$f" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
	[ "$t" -gt "$newest" ] && newest=$t
done

updater=none
if [ -d /run/systemd/system ] && command -v systemctl >/dev/null 2>&1; then
	for u in clamav-freshclam.service freshclam.service freshclam.timer; do
		if systemctl is-active --quiet "$u"; then updater=$u; break; fi
	done
elif command -v rc-service >/dev/null 2>&1 && rc-service freshclam status >/dev/null 2>&1; then
	updater="OpenRC freshclam"
fi
if [ "$updater" = none ] && grep -qs freshclam /etc/crontab /etc/cron.d/* /etc/crontabs/root /var/spool/cron/crontabs/root /var/spool/cron/root; then
	updater=cron
fi

if [ "$newest" -eq 0 ]; then
	echo "FAIL: no daily signature database in $dbdir"
	echo "$version"
	exit 1
fi
age=$((($(date +%s) - newest) / 86400))
detail="signatures ${age} day(s) old, automatic updates: $updater"

if [ "$age" -ge "$fail_days" ]; then
	echo "FAIL: $detail"; rc=1
elif [ "$age" -ge "$warn_days" ] || [ "$updater" = none ]; then
	echo "WARNING: $detail"; rc=2
else
	echo "OK: $detail"; rc=0
fi
echo "$version"
echo "Database: $dbdir, daily updated $(date -d "@$newest" '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M' 2>/dev/null || echo "$newest")"
exit $rc

variables.help: Signature age that counts as a warning.
variables.name: WARN_DAYS
variables.label: Warn at signature age (days)

variables.help: Signature age that fails the check.
variables.name: FAIL_DAYS
variables.label: Fail at signature age (days)

fields.name: ESET Endpoint Antivirus for Linux - install
fields.description: Installs ESET Endpoint Antivirus for Linux from your hosted .bin after a sha256 check, with the documented -y -f switches, and activates it.
fields.script_body:
#!/bin/sh
# Installs ESET Endpoint Antivirus for Linux or ESET Server Security for Linux from the vendor .bin installer
#   after checking its sha256, then activates it when a license key is given.
# Variables: PRODUCT (endpoint-antivirus) endpoint-antivirus or server-security; INSTALLER_URL ("" = vendor default,
#   required for endpoint-antivirus, https only); INSTALLER_SHA256 (required); LICENSE_KEY ("").
# Exit: 0 installed or already installed, 1 failed, 3 bad input or unsupported system.
PATH=/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin
export PATH
set -u

product=${PRODUCT:-endpoint-antivirus}
url=${INSTALLER_URL:-}
sha=$(printf '%s' "${INSTALLER_SHA256:-}" | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]')
key=${LICENSE_KEY:-}

case "$product" in
endpoint-antivirus) dir=/opt/eset/eea; name="ESET Endpoint Antivirus for Linux" ;;
server-security)
	dir=/opt/eset/efs; name="ESET Server Security for Linux"
	[ -n "$url" ] || url=https://download.eset.com/com/eset/apps/business/efs/linux/latest/efs.x86_64.bin
	;;
*) echo "PRODUCT must be endpoint-antivirus or server-security"; exit 3 ;;
esac
[ -n "$url" ] || { echo "INSTALLER_URL is required: ESET publishes the endpoint .bin only behind its download page"; exit 3; }
case "$url" in
https://*) ;;
*) echo "INSTALLER_URL must start with https://"; exit 3 ;;
esac
case "$url" in *[[:space:]\"\'\`]*) echo "INSTALLER_URL contains spaces or quotes"; exit 3 ;; esac
case "$sha" in
*[!0-9a-f]*) echo "INSTALLER_SHA256 must be 64 hex characters"; exit 3 ;;
esac
[ ${#sha} -eq 64 ] || { echo "INSTALLER_SHA256 must be 64 hex characters (sha256sum of the .bin)"; exit 3; }
case "$key" in
*[!A-Za-z0-9-]*) echo "LICENSE_KEY may only contain letters, digits and dashes"; exit 3 ;;
esac

[ "$(id -u)" -eq 0 ] || { echo "Must run as root"; exit 3; }
command -v sha256sum >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "sha256sum not found (package coreutils)"; exit 3; }
if command -v curl >/dev/null 2>&1; then
	fetch() { curl -fsSL --proto '=https' --proto-redir '=https' --tlsv1.2 --max-time 3600 -o "$2" "$1"; }
elif command -v wget >/dev/null 2>&1; then
	fetch() { wget -q --https-only -O "$2" "$1"; }
else
	echo "Neither curl nor wget found (install curl)"; exit 3
fi

if [ -x "$dir/sbin/lic" ]; then
	echo "Already installed: $name ($dir)"
else
	work=$(mktemp -d) || exit 1
	trap 'rm -rf "$work"' EXIT
	echo "Downloading $name from $(echo "$url" | cut -d/ -f3)"
	fetch "$url" "$work/installer.bin" || { echo "Download failed"; exit 1; }
	got=$(sha256sum "$work/installer.bin" | cut -d' ' -f1)
	if [ "$got" != "$sha" ]; then
		echo "sha256 mismatch, not run: got $got"
		exit 1
	fi
	echo "sha256 verified"
	# -y accepts the license agreement, -f skips the questions.
	out=$(sh "$work/installer.bin" -y -f 2>&1)
	rc=$?
	echo "$out" | tail -n 5
	if [ $rc -ne 0 ] || [ ! -x "$dir/sbin/lic" ]; then
		echo "Installation failed (exit $rc)"
		exit 1
	fi
	echo "Installed: $name"
fi

if [ -n "$key" ]; then
	if "$dir/sbin/lic" -k "$key" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
		echo "Activated with the given license key"
	else
		echo "Activation failed, check the key and the connection to ESET"
		exit 1
	fi
else
	echo "Not activated: set LICENSE_KEY, use ESET PROTECT or the web interface"
fi
exit 0

variables.help: https URL of eeau.x86_64.bin from ESET's download page.
variables.name: INSTALLER_URL
variables.label: Installer URL

variables.help: sha256sum of the .bin; the installer is not run when it differs.
variables.name: INSTALLER_SHA256
variables.label: Installer sha256

variables.help: ESET license key for lic -k, never printed. Empty leaves activation to ESET PROTECT.
variables.name: LICENSE_KEY
variables.label: License key

fields.name: Hardware identity collector
fields.description: Reads vendor, model and serial from sysfs DMI, dmidecode or the device tree. The last line is the serial number; exit 3 when the system has none.
fields.script_body:
#!/bin/sh
# Collects vendor, model and serial number (sysfs DMI, dmidecode, device tree). The last line is the serial.
# Variables: none
# Exit: 0 serial found, 3 no usable serial on this system (virtual machine, container or board without one)
PATH=/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin
export PATH LC_ALL=C
set -u

dmi() {
  v=$(cat "/sys/class/dmi/id/$1" 2>/dev/null)
  if [ -z "$v" ] && command -v dmidecode >/dev/null 2>&1; then v=$(dmidecode -s "$2" 2>/dev/null | head -n 1); fi
  printf '%s' "$v" | tr -d '\r\n' | sed 's/^[[:space:]]*//;s/[[:space:]]*$//'
}
junk() {
  case $(printf '%s' "$1" | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]') in
  '' | 0 | none | 'not specified' | 'not available' | 'to be filled by o.e.m.' | 'default string' | 'system serial number' | 'unknown' | 'n/a' | '0123456789' | '123456789' | 'chassis serial number') return 0 ;;
  esac
  return 1
}
vendor=$(dmi sys_vendor system-manufacturer)
model=$(dmi product_name system-product-name)
serial=$(dmi product_serial system-serial-number)
junk "$serial" && serial=$(dmi board_serial baseboard-serial-number)
junk "$serial" && serial=$(dmi chassis_serial chassis-serial-number)
if junk "$serial"; then
  serial=$(tr -d '\0' 2>/dev/null </proc/device-tree/serial-number)
  [ -n "$serial" ] || serial=$(sed -n 's/^Serial[[:space:]]*: *//p' /proc/cpuinfo 2>/dev/null | head -n 1)
fi
[ -n "$vendor" ] || vendor=$(tr -d '\0' 2>/dev/null </proc/device-tree/model)
echo "Vendor: ${vendor:-unknown}"
echo "Model: ${model:-unknown}"
echo "BIOS: $(dmi bios_vendor bios-vendor) $(dmi bios_version bios-version)"
if junk "$serial"; then
  echo "No serial number available (virtual machine, container or firmware without one)"
  exit 3
fi
echo "$serial"

fields.name: Kernel report
fields.description: Shows the running kernel, installed kernels, kernel packages and whether a newer one needs a reboot. Read only.
fields.script_body:
#!/bin/sh
# Reports the running kernel, the installed kernels and the newest one.
# Variables: none
# Exit: 0 report printed, 3 no kernel information on this system (container without module directory)
PATH=/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin
export PATH LC_ALL=C
set -u

run=$(uname -r)
echo "Running: $run"
dir=''
for d in /usr/lib/modules /lib/modules; do
  [ -d "$d" ] && [ -n "$(ls "$d" 2>/dev/null)" ] && { dir=$d; break; }
done
if [ -z "$dir" ]; then
  echo "Unsupported: no installed kernel found in /lib/modules (container?)"
  exit 3
fi
list=$(for k in "$dir"/*; do [ -e "$k" ] && echo "${k##*/}"; done | sort -V)
echo "Installed:"
printf '%s\n' "$list" | sed 's/^/  /'
newest=$(printf '%s\n' "$list" | tail -n 1)
echo "Newest installed: $newest"
if command -v dpkg >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  p=$(dpkg-query -W -f '${Package} ${Version}\n' 'linux-image-[0-9]*' 2>/dev/null)
elif command -v rpm >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  p=$(rpm -q kernel kernel-default kernel-core 2>/dev/null | grep -v 'not installed')
elif command -v pacman >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  p=$(pacman -Q 2>/dev/null | grep -E '^linux(-lts|-zen|-hardened)? ')
elif command -v apk >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  p=$(apk info -v 2>/dev/null | grep -E '^linux-(lts|virt|edge)-[0-9]')
else
  p=''
fi
[ -n "$p" ] && { echo "Packages:"; printf '%s\n' "$p" | sed 's/^/  /'; }
if [ "$newest" = "$run" ]; then echo "Reboot needed: no"; else echo "Reboot needed: yes (running $run, newest $newest)"; fi

fields.name: Listening ports report
fields.description: Lists listening TCP and UDP sockets with the owning process (ss, netstat, or /proc without process names). Read only.
fields.script_body:
#!/bin/sh
# Lists listening TCP and UDP sockets with the owning process (ss, netstat, or /proc without names).
# Variables: none
# Exit: 0 report printed, 3 no way to read sockets
PATH=/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin
export PATH LC_ALL=C
set -u
command -v awk >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "awk is not installed (install gawk or mawk)"; exit 3; }

if command -v ss >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "Proto Local address               Process"
  ss -H -l -n -t -u -p 2>/dev/null | awk '{p = ""; if (match($0, /users:\(\("[^"]*"/)) p = substr($0, RSTART + 9, RLENGTH - 9); gsub(/"/, "", p); printf "%-5s %-26s %s\n", $1, $5, p}' | sort -u
elif command -v netstat >/dev/null 2>&1 && netstat -ltnp >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "Proto Local address               Process"
  netstat -l -n -t -u -p 2>/dev/null | awk '$1 ~ /^(tcp|udp)/ {pid = $NF; if ($1 ~ /^udp/ && NF < 6) pid = "-"; printf "%-5s %-26s %s\n", $1, $4, pid}' | sort -u
elif [ -r /proc/net/tcp ]; then
  echo "Proto Port   (no ss or netstat installed: process names unavailable)"
  for f in tcp tcp6 udp udp6; do
    [ -r /proc/net/$f ] || continue
    awk -v pr="$f" '
      function hex(s,  i, v) { v = 0; for (i = 1; i <= length(s); i++) v = v * 16 + index("0123456789ABCDEF", toupper(substr(s, i, 1))) - 1; return v }
      NR > 1 && (($4 == "0A" && pr ~ /^tcp/) || ($4 == "07" && pr ~ /^udp/)) { n = split($2, a, ":"); printf "%-5s %s\n", pr, hex(a[n]) }' /proc/net/$f
  done | sort -u
else
  echo "Unsupported: no ss, netstat or /proc/net"
  exit 3
fi

fields.name: Logged-in users report
fields.description: Lists current logins, systemd sessions and the last ten logins. Read only.
fields.script_body:
#!/bin/sh
# Lists logged-in users and the most recent logins.
# Variables: none
# Exit: 0 report printed, 3 no tool to read login records
PATH=/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin
export PATH LC_ALL=C
set -u

have() { command -v "$1" >/dev/null 2>&1; }
have who || { echo "Unsupported: who is not installed (coreutils or busybox)"; exit 3; }
echo "Logged in now:"
w=$(who 2>/dev/null)
if [ -n "$w" ]; then printf '%s\n' "$w" | sed 's/^/  /'; else echo "  nobody"; fi
if have loginctl && [ -d /run/systemd/system ]; then
  echo "systemd sessions:"
  loginctl list-sessions --no-legend --no-pager 2>/dev/null | sed 's/^/  /'
fi
if have last; then
  echo "Recent logins:"
  last -n 10 2>/dev/null | grep -v '^$' | sed 's/^/  /'
else

fi

fields.name: Scheduled jobs report
fields.description: Lists system and per-user crontabs, cron.d, periodic directories, systemd timers and at jobs. Read only.
fields.script_body:
#!/bin/sh
# Lists scheduled jobs: system crontab, cron.d, per-user crontabs, periodic directories, systemd timers, at jobs.
# Variables: none
# Exit: 0 report printed
PATH=/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin
export PATH LC_ALL=C
set -u

show() {
  [ -r "$1" ] || return 0
  body=$(grep -v '^[[:space:]]*#' "$1" 2>/dev/null | grep -v '^[[:space:]]*$' | grep -Ev '^[A-Za-z_]+=')
  [ -n "$body" ] || return 0
  echo "== $1"
  printf '%s\n' "$body" | cut -c1-200 | sed 's/^/  /'
}
show /etc/crontab
for f in /etc/cron.d/*; do [ -f "$f" ] && show "$f"; done
for dir in /var/spool/cron/crontabs /var/spool/cron/tabs /var/spool/cron /etc/crontabs; do
  [ -d "$dir" ] || continue
  for f in "$dir"/*; do [ -f "$f" ] && show "$f"; done
done
echo "== periodic directories"
for d in hourly daily weekly monthly; do
  [ -d "/etc/cron.$d" ] && echo "  cron.$d: $(for j in "/etc/cron.$d"/*; do [ -e "$j" ] && printf '%s ' "${j##*/}"; done)"
done
[ -d /etc/periodic ] && for d in /etc/periodic/*; do [ -d "$d" ] && echo "  periodic/${d##*/}: $(for j in "$d"/*; do [ -e "$j" ] && printf '%s ' "${j##*/}"; done)"; done
if [ -d /run/systemd/system ] && command -v systemctl >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "== systemd timers"
  systemctl list-timers --all --no-pager --no-legend 2>/dev/null | cut -c1-160 | sed 's/^/  /'
fi
if command -v atq >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  a=$(atq 2>/dev/null)
  [ -n "$a" ] && { echo "== at jobs"; printf '%s\n' "$a" | sed 's/^/  /'; }
fi
exit 0

fields.name: System report
fields.description: Prints distribution, kernel, uptime, virtualization, CPU, memory, disks, filesystems, addresses, default route, package managers, service manager and pending reboot. Read only.
fields.script_body:
#!/bin/sh
# Prints a system summary: distribution, kernel, uptime, virtualization, CPU, memory, disks, addresses, routes.
# Variables: none
# Exit: 0 always (missing details are shown as unknown)
PATH=/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin
export PATH LC_ALL=C
set -u
command -v awk >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "awk is not installed (install gawk or mawk)"; exit 3; }

osr() { sed -n "s/^$1=//p" /etc/os-release /usr/lib/os-release 2>/dev/null | head -n 1 | tr -d '"'; }
have() { command -v "$1" >/dev/null 2>&1; }

echo "Host:           $(hostname 2>/dev/null || cat /proc/sys/kernel/hostname)"
echo "Distribution:   $(osr PRETTY_NAME)"
echo "Kernel:         $(uname -sr) $(uname -m)"
if [ -r /proc/uptime ]; then
  read -r up _ </proc/uptime
  echo "Uptime:         $((${up%%.*} / 86400)) days $((${up%%.*} % 86400 / 3600)) h"
fi

virt=''
have systemd-detect-virt && virt=$(systemd-detect-virt 2>/dev/null)
if [ -z "$virt" ] || [ "$virt" = none ]; then
  if [ -e /.dockerenv ]; then virt=docker
  elif grep -qs 'container=' /proc/1/environ 2>/dev/null; then virt=container
  elif grep -qs ' hypervisor' /proc/cpuinfo 2>/dev/null; then virt="vm ($(cat /sys/class/dmi/id/sys_vendor 2>/dev/null))"
  else virt=none; fi
fi
echo "Virtualization: $virt"

cpu=$(sed -n 's/^model name[[:space:]]*: *//p' /proc/cpuinfo 2>/dev/null | head -n 1)
[ -n "$cpu" ] || cpu=$(sed -n 's/^\(Hardware\|Model\)[[:space:]]*: *//p' /proc/cpuinfo 2>/dev/null | head -n 1)
echo "CPU:            ${cpu:-unknown}, $(grep -c '^processor' /proc/cpuinfo 2>/dev/null) logical"
mt=$(awk '$1 == "MemTotal:" {print int($2 / 1024)}' /proc/meminfo)
ma=$(awk '$1 == "MemAvailable:" {print int($2 / 1024)}' /proc/meminfo)
st=$(awk '$1 == "SwapTotal:" {print int($2 / 1024)}' /proc/meminfo)
echo "Memory:         ${mt:-?} MB total, ${ma:-?} MB available, swap ${st:-0} MB"

pm=''
for p in apt-get dnf yum zypper pacman apk; do have $p && { pm="$pm $p"; }; done
echo "Package mgr:   ${pm:- none found}"
if [ -d /run/systemd/system ]; then sm=systemd
elif [ -d /run/openrc ] || have rc-service; then sm=OpenRC
elif [ "$(cat /proc/1/comm 2>/dev/null)" = runit ]; then sm=runit
else sm="other ($(cat /proc/1/comm 2>/dev/null))"; fi
echo "Service mgr:    $sm"

rb=no
if [ -e /var/run/reboot-required ]; then rb=yes
elif have needs-restarting; then needs-restarting -r >/dev/null 2>&1; [ $? -eq 1 ] && rb=yes
elif have zypper; then zypper -q needs-rebooting >/dev/null 2>&1; [ $? -eq 102 ] && rb=yes
fi
echo "Reboot pending: $rb"

echo
echo "Disks:"
if have lsblk; then lsblk -d -n -o NAME,SIZE,TYPE,MODEL 2>/dev/null | sed 's/^/  /'
else awk 'NR > 2 && $4 !~ /[0-9]$/ {printf "  %s %.1f GB\n", $4, $3 / 1048576}' /proc/partitions; fi
echo "Filesystems:"
df -P -k 2>/dev/null | awk 'NR > 1 && $1 ~ /^\// {printf "  %-28s %8.1f GB %4s used  %s\n", $1, $2 / 1048576, $5, $6}'

echo
echo "Addresses:"
if have ip; then ip -o addr show 2>/dev/null | awk '$3 ~ /^inet/ && $2 != "lo" {print "  " $2 " " $4}'
elif have ifconfig; then ifconfig 2>/dev/null | awk '/^[a-z]/ {i = $1} /inet addr|inet / {print "  " i " " $0}'
else echo "  unknown (no ip or ifconfig)"; fi
echo "Default route:"
if have ip; then ip route show default 2>/dev/null | sed 's/^/  /'
else awk 'NR > 1 && $2 == "00000000" {printf "  via %s dev %s (hex, little endian)\n", $3, $1}' /proc/net/route; fi
exit 0

fields.name: Container prune
fields.description: Removes stopped containers, dangling images and unused networks of docker or podman and reports the space before and after. Dry run by default.
fields.script_body:
#!/bin/sh
# Removes stopped containers, dangling images and unused networks of docker or podman.
# Variables: DRY_RUN (default true), ALL_IMAGES (default false, also unused tagged images), VOLUMES (default false, also unused volumes).
# Exit codes: 0 done, 1 prune failed, 3 bad input or no container runtime.
PATH=/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin
export PATH
set -u

flag() {
  case $1 in true) echo 1 ;; false) echo 0 ;; *) echo "$2 must be true or false" >&2; exit 3 ;; esac
}
dry=$(flag "${DRY_RUN:-true}" DRY_RUN) || exit 3
all=$(flag "${ALL_IMAGES:-false}" ALL_IMAGES) || exit 3
vols=$(flag "${VOLUMES:-false}" VOLUMES) || exit 3
for r in docker podman; do
  command -v "$r" >/dev/null 2>&1 && rt=$r && break
done
[ -n "${rt:-}" ] || { echo "Neither docker nor podman is installed"; exit 3; }
"$rt" info >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "$rt is installed but its daemon is not reachable"; exit 3; }

echo "Before:"
"$rt" system df
if [ "$dry" = 1 ]; then
  echo "Dry run, would remove:"
  "$rt" ps -a --filter status=exited --filter status=created --format 'container {{.Names}} ({{.Image}})'
  if [ "$all" = 1 ]; then
    "$rt" images --filter dangling=false --format 'image {{.Repository}}:{{.Tag}} (all unused ones)'
  else
    "$rt" images --filter dangling=true --format 'dangling image {{.ID}}'
  fi
  [ "$vols" = 1 ] && "$rt" volume ls --filter dangling=true --format 'volume {{.Name}}'
  exit 0
fi
set -- system prune -f
[ "$all" = 1 ] && set -- "$@" -a
[ "$vols" = 1 ] && set -- "$@" --volumes
"$rt" "$@" >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "$rt prune failed"; exit 1; }
echo "After:"
"$rt" system df
exit 0

variables.help: Only list what would be removed.
variables.name: DRY_RUN
variables.label: Dry run

variables.help: Also remove tagged images no container uses.
variables.name: ALL_IMAGES
variables.label: All unused images

variables.help: Also remove volumes no container uses (data is lost).
variables.name: VOLUMES
variables.label: Unused volumes

fields.script_body:
#!/bin/sh
# Runs fstrim on all mounted filesystems that support it.
# Variables: none. Exit codes: 0 done, 1 trim failed, 3 fstrim missing or not possible here (container, no discard).
PATH=/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin
export PATH
set -u

command -v fstrim >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "fstrim not found: install util-linux"; exit 3; }
if [ -f /.dockerenv ] || grep -qaE 'docker|lxc|containerd|kubepods' /proc/1/cgroup 2>/dev/null; then
  echo "Running in a container, the host has to trim"
  exit 3
fi
out=$(fstrim -av 2>&1)
rc=$?
echo "$out"
if [ "$rc" -ne 0 ] && [ -z "$out" ]; then
  echo "No filesystem supports trim here"
  exit 3
fi
[ "$rc" -eq 0 ] || exit 1
exit 0

fields.name: Package cache clean
fields.description: Clears the package manager cache (apt, dnf, yum, zypper, pacman, apk) and reports the space freed. Exit 1 when cleaning fails, 3 without a package manager.
fields.script_body:
#!/bin/sh
# Cleans the package manager cache (apt, dnf, yum, zypper, pacman, apk) and reports the space freed.
# Variables: none. Exit codes: 0 done, 1 cleaning failed, 3 no supported package manager.
PATH=/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin
export PATH
set -u

size_kb() {
  t=0
  for d in /var/cache/apt /var/cache/dnf /var/cache/yum /var/cache/zypp /var/cache/pacman/pkg /var/cache/apk; do
    [ -d "$d" ] || continue
    k=$(du -sk "$d" 2>/dev/null | cut -f1)
    t=$((t + ${k:-0}))
  done
  echo "$t"
}

for c in apt-get dnf yum zypper pacman apk; do
  command -v "$c" >/dev/null 2>&1 && pm=$c && break
done
[ -n "${pm:-}" ] || { echo "No supported package manager found"; exit 3; }

before=$(size_kb)
case $pm in
apt-get) apt-get clean >/dev/null 2>&1 ;;
dnf) dnf -y clean all >/dev/null 2>&1 ;;
yum) yum -y clean all >/dev/null 2>&1 ;;
zypper) zypper -n clean --all >/dev/null 2>&1 ;;
pacman) yes | pacman -Scc >/dev/null 2>&1; [ -d /var/cache/pacman/pkg ] && find /var/cache/pacman/pkg -maxdepth 1 -type f -exec rm -f -- {} + ;;
apk) apk cache clean >/dev/null 2>&1; [ -d /var/cache/apk ] && find /var/cache/apk -maxdepth 1 -type f -exec rm -f -- {} + ;;
esac
rc=$?
after=$(size_kb)
if [ "$rc" -ne 0 ]; then
  echo "Cache clean failed with $pm (exit $rc)"
  exit 1
fi
echo "Package cache cleaned with $pm: $((before / 1024)) MB before, $((after / 1024)) MB after"
exit 0

fields.name: Remove unused packages
fields.description: Removes packages nothing depends on any more (apt, dnf, yum, zypper, pacman) and never the running kernel. Dry run by default. Alpine has nothing to remove.
fields.script_body:
#!/bin/sh
# Removes packages nothing depends on any more (apt, dnf, yum, zypper, pacman); never the running kernel.
# Variables: DRY_RUN (default true, only lists what would go).
# Exit codes: 0 done or nothing to do, 1 removal failed, 3 bad input or unsupported system.
PATH=/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin
export PATH
set -u

command -v awk >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "awk not found: install gawk"; exit 3; }

dry=${DRY_RUN:-true}
case $dry in true) ;; false) dry= ;; *) echo "DRY_RUN must be true or false"; exit 3 ;; esac
for c in apt-get dnf yum zypper pacman apk; do
  command -v "$c" >/dev/null 2>&1 && pm=$c && break
done
[ -n "${pm:-}" ] || { echo "No supported package manager found"; exit 3; }
kern=$(uname -r)
tmp=$(mktemp) || exit 1
trap 'rm -f "$tmp"' EXIT

case $pm in
apt-get)
  export DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive
  apt-get -s autoremove 2>/dev/null | sed -n 's/^Remv \([^ ]*\).*/\1/p' >"$tmp"
  if grep -qx "linux-image-$kern" "$tmp"; then
    echo "Refusing: the running kernel linux-image-$kern is on the removal list"
    exit 1
  fi
  n=$(wc -l <"$tmp")
  if [ -n "$dry" ] || [ "$n" -eq 0 ]; then
    echo "$n package(s) can be removed${dry:+ (dry run)}"
    cat "$tmp"
    exit 0
  fi
  apt-get -y -o DPkg::Lock::Timeout=300 autoremove >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "apt-get autoremove failed"; exit 1; }
  ;;
dnf | yum)
  $pm autoremove --assumeno 2>&1 | awk '/^[ ]*Removing( dependent packages)?:[ ]*$/ {f=1; next} /^[ ]*$/ {f=0} f && NF>=4 {print $1}' | sort -u >"$tmp"
  n=$(wc -l <"$tmp")
  if [ -n "$dry" ] || [ "$n" -eq 0 ]; then
    echo "$n package(s) can be removed${dry:+ (dry run)}"
    cat "$tmp"
    exit 0
  fi
  $pm -y autoremove >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "$pm autoremove failed"; exit 1; }
  ;;
zypper)
  zypper -n packages --unneeded 2>/dev/null | awk -F'|' '$1 ~ /i/ {gsub(/ /,"",$3); print $3}' |
    grep -E '^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9+._-]*$' | grep -v '^kernel' >"$tmp"
  n=$(wc -l <"$tmp")
  if [ -n "$dry" ] || [ "$n" -eq 0 ]; then
    echo "$n unneeded package(s)${dry:+ (dry run)}"
    cat "$tmp"
    exit 0
  fi
  # shellcheck disable=SC2046
  zypper -n remove --no-clean-deps $(cat "$tmp") >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "zypper remove failed"; exit 1; }
  ;;
pacman)
  pacman -Qdtq 2>/dev/null | grep -E '^[A-Za-z0-9@._+-]+$' >"$tmp"
  owner=$(pacman -Qqo "/usr/lib/modules/$kern/vmlinuz" 2>/dev/null)
  [ -n "$owner" ] && grep -vx "$owner" "$tmp" >"$tmp.2" && mv "$tmp.2" "$tmp"
  n=$(wc -l <"$tmp")
  if [ -n "$dry" ] || [ "$n" -eq 0 ]; then
    echo "$n orphan package(s)${dry:+ (dry run)}"
    cat "$tmp"
    exit 0
  fi
  # no -s: it would also take dependencies the dry run did not list
  # shellcheck disable=SC2046
  pacman -Rn --noconfirm $(cat "$tmp") >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "pacman remove failed"; exit 1; }
  ;;
apk)
  echo "apk has no unused-package concept, nothing to do"
  exit 0
  ;;
esac
echo "Unused packages removed with $pm"
exit 0

variables.label: Dry run
