fields.name: Temporary files clean
fields.description: Deletes files in /tmp and /var/tmp that were neither modified, read nor changed for the given number of days; files held open by a process are kept. Dry run by default.
fields.script_body:
#!/bin/sh
# Deletes files in /tmp and /var/tmp not modified, read or changed for MAX_AGE_DAYS days; open files are kept.
# Variables: DRY_RUN (default true, only lists), MAX_AGE_DAYS (default 10).
# Exit codes: 0 done, 1 cleaning failed, 3 bad input.
PATH=/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin
export PATH
set -u

command -v awk >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "awk not found: install gawk"; exit 3; }

dry=${DRY_RUN:-true}
case $dry in true) ;; false) dry= ;; *) echo "DRY_RUN must be true or false"; exit 3 ;; esac
age=${MAX_AGE_DAYS:-10}
case $age in '' | *[!0-9]*) echo "MAX_AGE_DAYS must be a whole number"; exit 3 ;; esac
[ ${#age} -le 5 ] && [ "$age" -ge 1 ] && [ "$age" -le 36500 ] || { echo "MAX_AGE_DAYS must be 1-36500"; exit 3; }

# files a running process holds open are kept
# shellcheck disable=SC2012
keep=$(ls -l /proc/[0-9]*/fd 2>/dev/null | awk -F' -> ' 'NF > 1 && $2 ~ /^\/(var\/)?tmp\// {print $2}' | sort -u |
  while IFS= read -r f; do i=$(stat -c %i "$f" 2>/dev/null) && printf '! -inum %s ' "$i"; done)
used_kb() { df -Pk /tmp /var/tmp 2>/dev/null | awk 'NR>1 {s+=$3} END {print s+0}'; }
# shellcheck disable=SC2086
list() {
  for d in /tmp /var/tmp; do
    [ -d "$d" ] && [ ! -L "$d" ] || continue
    find "$d" -xdev -mindepth 1 \
      \( -name 'systemd-private-*' -o -name '.X11-unix' -o -name '.ICE-unix' -o -name '.font-unix' \
      -o -name '.XIM-unix' -o -name '.Test-unix' -o -name '*ulrmm*' -o -name 'tmux-*' \) -prune -o \
      \( -type f -o -type l \) -mtime "+$age" -atime "+$age" -ctime "+$age" $keep "$@"
  done
}

tmp=$(mktemp) || exit 1
trap 'rm -f "$tmp"' EXIT
list -print >"$tmp"
n=$(wc -l <"$tmp")
if [ -n "$dry" ]; then
  echo "Dry run: $n file(s) older than $age days"
  head -50 "$tmp"
  exit 0
fi
before=$(used_kb)
# -execdir works from the file's directory, so a directory swapped for a symlink cannot redirect rm
# (busybox find has no -execdir)
if find / -maxdepth 0 -execdir true {} + >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  list -execdir rm -f -- {} + 2>/dev/null
else
  list -exec rm -f -- {} + 2>/dev/null
fi
for d in /tmp /var/tmp; do
  [ -d "$d" ] && [ ! -L "$d" ] && find "$d" -xdev -mindepth 1 -type d -empty -mtime "+$age" \
    ! -path '*/systemd-private-*' ! -path '*/.*-unix*' ! -path '*ulrmm*' ! -path '*/tmux-*' -delete 2>/dev/null
done
after=$(used_kb)
echo "Removed $n file(s) older than $age days, freed about $(((before - after) / 1024)) MB"
exit 0

fields.script_body:
#!/bin/sh
# Finds unhealthy, restarting and non-zero-exited containers (docker or podman).
# Variables: IGNORE (container names to skip, comma or line separated, optional)
# Exit: 0 all fine, 1 problem containers found, 3 bad input or no container engine
PATH=/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin
export PATH LC_ALL=C
set -u

IGN=$(printf '%s\n' "${IGNORE:-}" | tr ',' '\n' | sed 's/^[[:space:]]*//;s/[[:space:]]*$//;/^$/d')
case $(printf %s "$IGN" | tr -d "\n") in *[!A-Za-z0-9_.-]* | -*) echo "IGNORE has characters that are not allowed in a container name"; exit 3 ;; esac

eng=''
for e in docker podman; do command -v $e >/dev/null 2>&1 && { eng=$e; break; }; done
[ -n "$eng" ] || { echo "Unsupported: neither docker nor podman is installed"; exit 3; }
list=$($eng ps -a --format '{{.Names}}|{{.State}}|{{.Status}}' 2>&1) || { echo "Cannot reach $eng: $(printf '%s' "$list" | head -n 1)"; exit 3; }

nl='
'
bad='' n=0
while IFS='|' read -r name state status; do
  [ -n "$name" ] || continue
  n=$((n + 1))
  [ -n "$IGN" ] && printf '%s\n' "$IGN" | grep -qxF -- "$name" && continue
  case $status in
  *unhealthy*) bad="$bad$name: unhealthy ($status)$nl" ;;
  *) case $state in
     restarting) bad="$bad$name: restarting ($status)$nl" ;;
     exited | stopped) case $status in 'Exited (0)'*) ;; *) bad="$bad$name: $status$nl" ;; esac ;;
     esac ;;
  esac
done <<EOT
$list
EOT
if [ -z "$bad" ]; then
  echo "OK: $n containers, none unhealthy, restarting or failed ($eng)"
  exit 0
fi
echo "ERROR: $(printf '%s' "$bad" | wc -l) of $n containers need attention ($eng)"
printf '%s' "$bad"
exit 1

fields.name: Disk space check
fields.description: Checks used space on local filesystems (ext4, xfs, btrfs, zfs, vfat...) and skips tmpfs, overlay, squashfs and network mounts. Exit 2 at the warning level, 1 at the error level, 3 on bad input.
fields.script_body:
#!/bin/sh
# Checks used space on local filesystems against warning and error thresholds.
# Variables: WARN_PERCENT (85), ERROR_PERCENT (95), EXCLUDE (mount points, comma or line separated, optional)
# Exit: 0 ok, 1 error threshold reached, 2 warning threshold reached, 3 bad input or unsupported system
PATH=/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin
export PATH
set -u

int() {
  case $2 in '' | *[!0-9]*) echo "$1 must be a whole number"; exit 3 ;; esac
  { [ "${#2}" -le 3 ] && [ "$2" -ge 1 ] && [ "$2" -le 100 ]; } || { echo "$1 must be between 1 and 100"; exit 3; }
}
WARN=${WARN_PERCENT:-85}
ERR=${ERROR_PERCENT:-95}
int WARN_PERCENT "$WARN"
int ERROR_PERCENT "$ERR"
[ "$WARN" -lt "$ERR" ] || { echo "WARN_PERCENT must be lower than ERROR_PERCENT"; exit 3; }
EXC=$(printf '%s\n' "${EXCLUDE:-}" | tr ',' '\n' | sed 's/^[[:space:]]*//;s/[[:space:]]*$//;/^$/d')
case $(printf %s "$EXC" | tr -d "\n") in *[!A-Za-z0-9/._+@-]*) echo "EXCLUDE has characters that are not allowed in a mount point"; exit 3 ;; esac
[ -r /proc/mounts ] || { echo "Unsupported: /proc/mounts not readable"; exit 3; }

nl='
'
seen='|' detail='' worst=0 n=0 status=0 bad=''
while read -r dev mp fs _; do
  case $fs in ext2 | ext3 | ext4 | xfs | btrfs | zfs | f2fs | jfs | reiserfs | vfat | exfat | ntfs | ntfs3 | fuseblk | ufs | bcachefs) ;; *) continue ;; esac
  case $seen in *"|$dev|"*) continue ;; esac
  seen="$seen$dev|"
  mp=$(printf '%b' "$mp")
  printf '%s\n' "$EXC" | grep -qxF -- "$mp" && continue
  line=$(df -P -k "$mp" 2>/dev/null | tail -n 1)
  pct=''
  read -r _ _ _ _ pct _ <<EOT
$line
EOT
  pct=${pct%\%}
  case $pct in '' | *[!0-9]*) continue ;; esac
  n=$((n + 1))
  [ "$pct" -gt "$worst" ] && worst=$pct
  mark=ok
  if [ "$pct" -ge "$ERR" ]; then mark=ERROR; status=1
  elif [ "$pct" -ge "$WARN" ]; then mark=WARN; [ $status -eq 0 ] && status=2; fi
  [ $mark != ok ] && bad="$bad $mp:$pct%"
  detail="$detail$(printf '%-5s %3s%%  %s (%s, %s)' "$mark" "$pct" "$mp" "$fs" "$dev")$nl"
done </proc/mounts

[ $n -gt 0 ] || { echo "No local filesystems to check"; exit 3; }
case $status in
0) echo "OK: $n filesystems, highest use $worst%" ;;
1) echo "ERROR: at or above $ERR%:$bad" ;;
2) echo "WARNING: at or above $WARN%:$bad" ;;
esac
printf '%s' "$detail"
exit $status

fields.name: Failed logins report
fields.description: Counts failed SSH logins in the last hours from journald or auth.log/secure and lists the top source addresses. Exit 2 when the threshold is reached.
fields.script_body:
#!/bin/sh
# Counts failed SSH logins of the last HOURS hours and shows the top sources.
# Variables: HOURS (24), THRESHOLD (50, failures that count as a warning)
# Exit: 0 below threshold, 2 threshold reached, 3 bad input or no log source
PATH=/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin
export PATH LC_ALL=C
set -u
command -v awk >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "awk is not installed (install gawk or mawk)"; exit 3; }

int() {
  case $2 in '' | *[!0-9]*) echo "$1 must be a whole number"; exit 3 ;; esac
  { [ "${#2}" -le 6 ] && [ "$2" -ge 1 ] && [ "$2" -le "$3" ]; } || { echo "$1 must be between 1 and $3"; exit 3; }
}
H=${HOURS:-24}
T=${THRESHOLD:-50}
int HOURS "$H" 168
int THRESHOLD "$T" 1000000

pat='Failed password|Failed publickey|Failed keyboard-interactive|Invalid user'
if [ -d /run/systemd/system ] && command -v journalctl >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  src=journald
  out=$(journalctl -t sshd -t sshd-session -q --no-pager --since "$H hours ago" 2>/dev/null | grep -E "$pat")
else
  f=''
  for c in /var/log/auth.log /var/log/secure; do [ -r "$c" ] && { f=$c; break; }; done
  [ -n "$f" ] || { echo "Unsupported: no journald and no /var/log/auth.log or /var/log/secure"; exit 3; }
  src=$f
  now=$(date +%s)
  pats='|' h=0
  while [ "$h" -le "$H" ]; do
    s=$(date -d "@$((now - h * 3600))" '+%b %e %H|%Y-%m-%dT%H' 2>/dev/null) || { echo "Unsupported: date cannot convert epoch times"; exit 3; }
    pats="$pats${s%|*}|${s#*|}|"
    h=$((h + 1))
  done
  out=$(awk -v p="$pats" 'index(p, "|" substr($0, 1, 9) "|") || index(p, "|" substr($0, 1, 13) "|")' "$f" | grep -E "$pat")
fi
n=$(printf '%s' "$out" | grep -c .)
if [ "$n" -ge "$T" ]; then v="WARNING"; rc=2; else v="OK"; rc=0; fi
echo "$v: $n failed SSH logins in the last $H hours (threshold $T, $src)"
if [ "$n" -gt 0 ]; then
  echo "Top sources:"
  printf '%s\n' "$out" | sed -n 's/.* from \([0-9A-Fa-f.:]*\)\( port.*\)\{0,1\}$/\1/p' | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn | head -n 5
fi
exit $rc

variables.label: Warning threshold

#!/bin/sh
# Reports error-level log entries of the last HOURS hours (journald, else /var/log/messages or syslog).

PATH=/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin

command -v awk >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "awk is not installed (install gawk or mawk)"; exit 3; }

int() {
  case $2 in '' | *[!0-9]*) echo "$1 must be a whole number"; exit 3 ;; esac
  { [ "${#2}" -le 4 ] && [ "$2" -ge 1 ] && [ "$2" -le "$3" ]; } || { echo "$1 must be between 1 and $3"; exit 3; }
}
H=${HOURS:-24}
M=${MAX:-30}
int HOURS "$H" 168
int MAX "$M" 500

if [ -d /run/systemd/system ] && command -v journalctl >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  src=journald
  out=$(journalctl -p err -q --no-pager --since "$H hours ago" 2>/dev/null)
else
  f=''
  for c in /var/log/messages /var/log/syslog; do [ -r "$c" ] && { f=$c; break; }; done
  [ -n "$f" ] || { echo "Unsupported: no journald and no /var/log/messages or /var/log/syslog"; exit 3; }
  src=$f
  now=$(date +%s)
  pats='|' h=0
  while [ "$h" -le "$H" ]; do
    s=$(date -d "@$((now - h * 3600))" '+%b %e %H|%Y-%m-%dT%H' 2>/dev/null) || { echo "Unsupported: date cannot convert epoch times"; exit 3; }
    pats="$pats${s%|*}|${s#*|}|"
    h=$((h + 1))
  done
  out=$(awk -v p="$pats" 'index(p, "|" substr($0, 1, 9) "|") || index(p, "|" substr($0, 1, 13) "|")' "$f" | grep -Ei 'error|fail|critical|fatal|panic' )

fields.name: Listening port check
fields.description: Checks that every listed port has a listener, read from /proc/net so no extra tool is needed. Exit 1 when a port is closed.
fields.script_body:
#!/bin/sh
# Checks that every listed port has a listener (read from /proc/net, no extra tools needed).
# Variables: PORTS (1-65535, optionally prefixed tcp: or udp:, default tcp; comma or line separated, required)
# Exit: 0 all listening, 1 at least one port closed, 3 bad input
PATH=/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin
export PATH
set -u
command -v awk >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "awk is not installed (install gawk or mawk)"; exit 3; }

LIST=$(printf '%s\n' "${PORTS:-}" | tr ',' '\n' | sed 's/^[[:space:]]*//;s/[[:space:]]*$//;/^$/d')
[ -n "$LIST" ] || { echo "PORTS is required"; exit 3; }
for p in $LIST; do
  case $p in tcp:* | udp:*) num=${p#*:} ;; *) num=$p ;; esac
  case $num in '' | *[!0-9]*) echo "Bad port: $p"; exit 3 ;; esac
  { [ "${#num}" -le 5 ] && [ "$num" -ge 1 ] && [ "$num" -le 65535 ]; } || { echo "Port out of range: $p"; exit 3; }
done
[ -r /proc/net/tcp ] || { echo "Unsupported: /proc/net/tcp not readable"; exit 3; }

# listening sockets as proto:port lines
open=$(
  for f in tcp tcp6 udp udp6; do
    [ -r /proc/net/$f ] || continue
    awk -v pr="${f%6}" '
      function hex(s,  i, v, c) { v = 0; for (i = 1; i <= length(s); i++) { c = index("0123456789ABCDEF", toupper(substr(s, i, 1))) - 1; v = v * 16 + c } return v }
      NR > 1 && (($4 == "0A" && pr == "tcp") || ($4 == "07" && pr == "udp")) { n = split($2, a, ":"); print pr ":" hex(a[n]) }' /proc/net/$f
  done | sort -u
)
nl='
'
down='' up=0 n=0
for p in $LIST; do
  n=$((n + 1))
  case $p in tcp:* | udp:*) k=$p ;; *) k=tcp:$p ;; esac
  if printf '%s\n' "$open" | grep -qxF -- "$k"; then up=$((up + 1)); else down="$down$k: nothing listening$nl"; fi
done
if [ -z "$down" ]; then
  echo "OK: $up of $n ports listening"
  exit 0
fi
echo "ERROR: $((n - up)) of $n ports not listening"
printf '%s' "$down"
exit 1

variables.name: PORTS
variables.label: Ports

#!/bin/sh
# Checks used memory (from MemAvailable) against thresholds and reports swap.
# Variables: WARN_PERCENT (85), ERROR_PERCENT (95)
# Exit: 0 ok, 1 error threshold reached, 2 warning threshold reached, 3 bad input or unsupported system
PATH=/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin
export PATH
set -u

int() {
  case $2 in '' | *[!0-9]*) echo "$1 must be a whole number"; exit 3 ;; esac
  { [ "${#2}" -le 3 ] && [ "$2" -ge 1 ] && [ "$2" -le 100 ]; } || { echo "$1 must be between 1 and 100"; exit 3; }
}
WARN=${WARN_PERCENT:-85}
ERR=${ERROR_PERCENT:-95}
int WARN_PERCENT "$WARN"
int ERROR_PERCENT "$ERR"
[ "$WARN" -lt "$ERR" ] || { echo "WARN_PERCENT must be lower than ERROR_PERCENT"; exit 3; }

mi() { sed -n "s/^$1:[[:space:]]*\([0-9]*\).*/\1/p" /proc/meminfo 2>/dev/null; }
total=$(mi MemTotal)
avail=$(mi MemAvailable)
[ -n "$total" ] && [ -n "$avail" ] || { echo "Unsupported: MemTotal/MemAvailable missing in /proc/meminfo"; exit 3; }
swt=$(mi SwapTotal)
swf=$(mi SwapFree)
used=$((total - avail))
pct=$((used * 100 / total))
mb() { echo $(($1 / 1024)); }
if [ "${swt:-0}" -gt 0 ]; then
  swinfo="swap $(mb $((swt - swf))) of $(mb "$swt") MB used ($(((swt - swf) * 100 / swt))%)"
else
  swinfo="no swap"
fi
msg="$pct% used ($(mb $used) of $(mb "$total") MB, $(mb "$avail") MB available), $swinfo"
if [ "$pct" -ge "$ERR" ]; then echo "ERROR: memory $msg"; exit 1; fi
if [ "$pct" -ge "$WARN" ]; then echo "WARNING: memory $msg"; exit 2; fi
echo "OK: memory $msg"

variables.label: Warn at or above (%)

fields.description: Looks for kernel out-of-memory kills in the last hours (journald, else the kernel ring buffer since boot or kern.log). Exit 1 when any are found.
fields.script_body:
#!/bin/sh
# Looks for out-of-memory kills in the kernel log of the last HOURS hours.
# Variables: HOURS (24)
# Exit: 0 none found, 1 OOM kills found, 3 bad input or no kernel log source
PATH=/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin
export PATH LC_ALL=C
set -u

H=${HOURS:-24}
case $H in '' | *[!0-9]*) echo "HOURS must be a whole number"; exit 3 ;; esac
{ [ "${#H}" -le 4 ] && [ "$H" -ge 1 ] && [ "$H" -le 720 ]; } || { echo "HOURS must be between 1 and 720"; exit 3; }

pat='out of memory: kill|oom-kill:|invoked oom-killer|oom_reaper'
if [ -d /run/systemd/system ] && command -v journalctl >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  src=journald
  win="$H hours"
  out=$(journalctl -k -q --no-pager --since "$H hours ago" 2>/dev/null | grep -Ei "$pat")
else
  win='no time filter'
  # no timestamps in the ring buffer without journald: whole buffer since boot, say so
  src=''
  out=''
  if d=$(dmesg 2>/dev/null); then
    src="kernel ring buffer since boot"
    out=$(printf '%s\n' "$d" | grep -Ei "$pat")
  fi
  if [ -z "$out" ]; then
    for c in /var/log/kern.log /var/log/messages; do
      [ -r "$c" ] && { src=$c; out=$(grep -Ei "$pat" "$c" | tail -n 200); break; }
    done
  fi
  [ -n "$src" ] || { echo "Unsupported: no journald, no readable dmesg and no kernel log file"; exit 3; }
fi
n=$(printf '%s' "$out" | grep -c .)
if [ "$n" -eq 0 ]; then
  echo "OK: no out-of-memory kills found ($src, $win)"
  exit 0
fi
echo "ERROR: $n out-of-memory log entries ($src, $win)"
printf '%s\n' "$out" | tail -n 20 | cut -c1-300
exit 1

fields.name: Process running check
fields.description: Checks that every listed process name is running, using the kernel process name (15 characters). Exit 1 when one is missing.
fields.script_body:
#!/bin/sh
# Checks that every listed process name is running (matches the kernel process name, max 15 characters).
# Variables: PROCESSES (names, comma or line separated, required)
# Exit: 0 all running, 1 at least one not running, 3 bad input
PATH=/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin
export PATH
set -u

LIST=$(printf '%s\n' "${PROCESSES:-}" | tr ',' '\n' | sed 's/^[[:space:]]*//;s/[[:space:]]*$//;/^$/d')
[ -n "$LIST" ] || { echo "PROCESSES is required"; exit 3; }
case $(printf %s "$LIST" | tr -d "\n") in *[!A-Za-z0-9._+:@-]* | -*) echo "PROCESSES: names may only contain letters, digits and ._+:@- and no spaces"; exit 3 ;; esac
printf '%s\n' "$LIST" | grep -q '^-' && { echo "A process name must not start with a dash"; exit 3; }
[ -r /proc/self/comm ] || { echo "Unsupported: /proc not available"; exit 3; }

names=$(cat /proc/[0-9]*/comm 2>/dev/null)
nl='
'
down='' up=0 n=0
for p in $LIST; do
  n=$((n + 1))
  k=$(printf '%s' "$p" | cut -c1-15)
  c=$(printf '%s\n' "$names" | grep -cxF -- "$k")
  if [ "$c" -gt 0 ]; then up=$((up + 1)); else down="$down$p: not running$nl"; fi
done
if [ -z "$down" ]; then
  echo "OK: $up of $n processes running"
  exit 0
fi
echo "ERROR: $((n - up)) of $n processes not running"
printf '%s' "$down"
exit 1

variables.help: Process names such as nginx. One per line or comma separated.
variables.name: PROCESSES
variables.label: Processes

fields.name: Reboot required check
fields.description: Detects a pending reboot: Debian/Ubuntu flag file, needs-restarting on RHEL and Fedora, zypper needs-rebooting on openSUSE, otherwise running versus newest installed kernel. Exit 2 when a reboot is needed.
fields.script_body:
#!/bin/sh
# Reports whether a reboot is pending: package manager flag first, then running vs newest installed kernel.
# Variables: none
# Exit: 0 no reboot needed, 2 reboot required, 3 cannot be determined on this system
PATH=/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin
export PATH
set -u

if [ -e /var/run/reboot-required ]; then
  pk=$(tr '\n' ' ' 2>/dev/null </var/run/reboot-required.pkgs)
  echo "WARNING: reboot required${pk:+ by: $pk}"
  exit 2
fi
rc=''
if command -v needs-restarting >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  needs-restarting -r >/dev/null 2>&1
  rc=$?
elif command -v dnf >/dev/null 2>&1 && dnf needs-restarting --help >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  dnf -q needs-restarting -r >/dev/null 2>&1
  rc=$?
fi
case $rc in
0) echo "OK: no reboot required (needs-restarting)"; exit 0 ;;
1) echo "WARNING: reboot required (needs-restarting -r)"; exit 2 ;;
esac
if command -v zypper >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  zypper -q needs-rebooting >/dev/null 2>&1
  case $? in
  0) echo "OK: no reboot required (zypper needs-rebooting)"; exit 0 ;;
  102) echo "WARNING: reboot required (zypper needs-rebooting)"; exit 2 ;;
  esac
fi

run=$(uname -r)
dir=''
for d in /usr/lib/modules /lib/modules; do
  [ -d "$d" ] && [ -n "$(ls "$d" 2>/dev/null)" ] && { dir=$d; break; }
done
if [ -z "$dir" ]; then
  echo "Cannot determine: no package manager flag and no kernel modules directory (container?)"
  exit 3
fi
if [ ! -d "$dir/$run" ]; then
  echo "WARNING: reboot required, running kernel $run is no longer installed"
  exit 2
fi
newest=$(for k in "$dir"/*; do [ -e "$k" ] && echo "${k##*/}"; done | sort -V | tail -n 1)
if [ "$newest" != "$run" ]; then
  echo "WARNING: reboot required, running kernel $run, newest installed $newest"
  exit 2
fi
echo "OK: running the newest installed kernel $run"

fields.name: Services running check
fields.description: Checks that every listed service is active (systemd) or started (OpenRC). Exit 1 when one is not running.
fields.script_body:
#!/bin/sh
# Checks that every listed service is running (systemd or OpenRC).
# Variables: SERVICES (service names, comma or line separated, required)
# Exit: 0 all running, 1 at least one not running, 3 bad input or no supported service manager
PATH=/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin
export PATH
set -u

LIST=$(printf '%s\n' "${SERVICES:-}" | tr ',' '\n' | sed 's/^[[:space:]]*//;s/[[:space:]]*$//;/^$/d')
[ -n "$LIST" ] || { echo "SERVICES is required"; exit 3; }
case $(printf %s "$LIST" | tr -d "\n") in *[!A-Za-z0-9@._:\\-]* | -*) echo "SERVICES has characters that are not allowed in a service name"; exit 3 ;; esac
if printf '%s\n' "$LIST" | grep -q '^-'; then echo "A service name must not start with a dash"; exit 3; fi
printf '%s\n' "$LIST" | grep -q '[[:space:]]' && { echo "A service name must not contain spaces"; exit 3; }

if [ -d /run/systemd/system ] && command -v systemctl >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  mgr=systemd
elif command -v rc-service >/dev/null 2>&1 && [ -d /run/openrc ]; then
  mgr=OpenRC
else
  echo "Unsupported: neither a running systemd nor OpenRC found"
  exit 3
fi

nl='
'
down='' up=0 n=0
for s in $LIST; do
  n=$((n + 1))
  if [ $mgr = systemd ]; then
    case $s in *.*) u=$s ;; *) u=$s.service ;; esac
    st=$(systemctl is-active -- "$u" 2>/dev/null)
    [ "$st" = active ] && { up=$((up + 1)); continue; }
    down="$down$s: ${st:-unknown}$nl"
  else
    if rc-service -- "$s" status >/dev/null 2>&1; then up=$((up + 1)); else down="$down$s: not started$nl"; fi
  fi
done
if [ -z "$down" ]; then
  echo "OK: $up of $n services running ($mgr)"
  exit 0
fi
echo "ERROR: $((n - up)) of $n services not running ($mgr)"
printf '%s' "$down"
exit 1

variables.help: Service names such as sshd or cron. One per line or comma separated.
variables.name: SERVICES
variables.label: Services

fields.name: Time sync check
fields.description: Checks clock synchronisation with chrony, ntpd, systemd-timesyncd or busybox ntpd, whichever is present. Exit 1 when not synchronised, 3 when no tool exists.
fields.script_body:
#!/bin/sh
# Checks that the clock is synchronised (chrony, ntpd/ntpq, systemd-timesyncd or busybox ntpd).
# Variables: none
# Exit: 0 synchronised, 1 not synchronised, 3 no time sync tool found
PATH=/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin
export PATH LC_ALL=C
set -u

if command -v chronyc >/dev/null 2>&1 && t=$(chronyc tracking 2>/dev/null) && [ -n "$t" ]; then
  ref=$(printf '%s\n' "$t" | sed -n 's/^Reference ID *: *\([0-9A-Fa-f]*\).*/\1/p')
  off=$(printf '%s\n' "$t" | sed -n 's/^System time *: *\(.*\)/\1/p')
  case $ref in 0 | 00000000 | '') echo "ERROR: chrony has no time source ($off)"; exit 1 ;; esac
  case $(printf '%s\n' "$t" | sed -n 's/^Leap status *: *//p') in 'Not synchronised') echo "ERROR: chrony not synchronised"; exit 1 ;; esac
  echo "OK: chrony synchronised, offset $off"
  exit 0
fi
if command -v ntpq >/dev/null 2>&1 && p=$(ntpq -pn 2>/dev/null) && [ -n "$p" ]; then
  peer=$(printf '%s\n' "$p" | sed -n 's/^\*\([^ ]*\).*/\1/p' | head -n 1)
  [ -n "$peer" ] && { echo "OK: ntpd synchronised to $peer"; exit 0; }
  echo "ERROR: ntpd running but has no selected peer"
  exit 1
fi
if command -v timedatectl >/dev/null 2>&1 && [ -d /run/systemd/system ]; then
  s=$(timedatectl show -p NTPSynchronized --value 2>/dev/null)
  [ -n "$s" ] || s=$(timedatectl 2>/dev/null | sed -n 's/^ *System clock synchronized: *//p;s/^ *NTP synchronized: *//p' | head -n 1)
  case $s in
  yes) echo "OK: clock synchronised (systemd)"; exit 0 ;;
  no) echo "ERROR: clock not synchronised (systemd; is systemd-timesyncd or chrony enabled?)"; exit 1 ;;
  esac
fi
for d in /proc/[0-9]*; do
  [ "$(cat "$d/comm" 2>/dev/null)" = ntpd ] && { echo "OK: busybox ntpd is running (it cannot report its sync state)"; exit 0; }
done
echo "Unsupported: no chronyc, ntpq, timedatectl or running ntpd (install chrony)"
exit 3

fields.name: Uptime check
fields.description: Warns when the machine has been up longer than the limit, a hint for missed reboots after kernel updates. Exit 2 above the limit.
fields.script_body:
#!/bin/sh
# Warns when the machine has been up longer than MAX_DAYS (pending reboots, kernel updates).
# Variables: MAX_DAYS (60)
# Exit: 0 ok, 2 up longer than MAX_DAYS, 3 bad input or unsupported system
PATH=/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin
export PATH
set -u

MAX=${MAX_DAYS:-60}
case $MAX in '' | *[!0-9]*) echo "MAX_DAYS must be a whole number"; exit 3 ;; esac
{ [ "${#MAX}" -le 5 ] && [ "$MAX" -ge 1 ]; } || { echo "MAX_DAYS must be between 1 and 99999"; exit 3; }
[ -r /proc/uptime ] || { echo "Unsupported: /proc/uptime not readable"; exit 3; }
read -r up _ </proc/uptime
secs=${up%%.*}
days=$((secs / 86400))
hours=$((secs % 86400 / 3600))
if [ "$days" -ge "$MAX" ]; then
  echo "WARNING: up $days days $hours h, limit is $MAX days"
  exit 2
fi
echo "OK: up $days days $hours h, limit is $MAX days"

variables.help: Days of uptime that count as a warning.
variables.name: MAX_DAYS
variables.label: Maximum uptime (days)

fields.name: URL check
fields.description: Requests an http or https URL with curl or wget and compares the status code. Redirects are not followed with curl. Exit 1 on another status or no answer.
fields.script_body:
#!/bin/sh
# Requests a URL (no redirects followed with curl) and compares the HTTP status.
# Variables: URL (http or https, required), EXPECT_STATUS (200), TIMEOUT (10, seconds)
# Exit: 0 status as expected, 1 other status or no answer, 3 bad input or neither curl nor wget installed
PATH=/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin
export PATH LC_ALL=C
set -u

U=${URL:-}
[ -n "$U" ] || { echo "URL is required"; exit 3; }
case $U in http://* | https://*) ;; *) echo "URL must start with http:// or https://"; exit 3 ;; esac
case $U in *[!A-Za-z0-9._~:/?#@!\&=+,\;%-]*) echo "URL contains characters that are not allowed (spaces, quotes, \$, backslash...)"; exit 3 ;; esac
E=${EXPECT_STATUS:-200}
case $E in [1-5][0-9][0-9]) ;; *) echo "EXPECT_STATUS must be a 3 digit HTTP status"; exit 3 ;; esac
T=${TIMEOUT:-10}
case $T in '' | *[!0-9]*) echo "TIMEOUT must be a whole number"; exit 3 ;; esac
{ [ "${#T}" -le 3 ] && [ "$T" -ge 1 ] && [ "$T" -le 300 ]; } || { echo "TIMEOUT must be between 1 and 300"; exit 3; }

if command -v curl >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  r=$(curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code} %{time_total}' --max-time "$T" -- "$U" 2>&1); rc=$?
  if [ $rc -ne 0 ]; then echo "ERROR: $U no answer: $(printf '%s' "$r" | head -n 1 | cut -c1-150)"; exit 1; fi
  code=${r%% *}; secs=${r#* }
elif command -v wget >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  mr=''
  wget --help 2>&1 | grep -q 'max-redirect' && mr=--max-redirect=0
  # shellcheck disable=SC2086
  r=$(wget -S -q -O /dev/null -T "$T" $mr "$U" 2>&1) || true
  code=$(printf '%s\n' "$r" | sed -n 's/^ *HTTP\/[0-9.]* \([0-9][0-9][0-9]\).*/\1/p' | tail -n 1)
  if [ -z "$code" ]; then
    m=$(printf '%s' "$r" | tail -n 1 | cut -c1-150)
    echo "ERROR: $U no answer: ${m:-connection failed or timed out}"
    exit 1
  fi
  secs='?'
else
  echo "Unsupported: neither curl nor wget is installed (install curl)"
  exit 3
fi
if [ "$code" = "$E" ]; then echo "OK: $U returned $code in ${secs}s"; exit 0; fi
echo "ERROR: $U returned $code, expected $E (${secs}s)"
exit 1

variables.help: http:// or https:// address.
variables.name: URL
variables.label: URL

variables.help: HTTP status code that counts as healthy.
variables.name: EXPECT_STATUS
variables.label: Expected status

variables.help: Seconds to wait, 1 to 300.
variables.name: TIMEOUT
variables.label: Timeout (s)

fields.description: Pings hosts, opens TCP connections to host:port targets and optionally resolves a name. Exit 1 when any test fails.

variables.help: host or host:port. One per line or comma separated.
variables.name: TARGETS

fields.name: DNS report
fields.description: Shows resolver configuration (resolv.conf, systemd-resolved, nsswitch) and runs test lookups. Exit 1 when example.com cannot be resolved.
fields.script_body:
#!/bin/sh
# Reports the DNS resolver setup (resolv.conf, systemd-resolved, nsswitch) and runs test lookups.
# Variables: none
# Exit: 0 lookups work, 1 the public test lookup failed, 3 no resolver configuration and no lookup tool
PATH=/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin
export PATH LC_ALL=C
set -u
command -v awk >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "awk is not installed (install gawk or mawk)"; exit 3; }

have() { command -v "$1" >/dev/null 2>&1; }
[ -r /etc/resolv.conf ] || have getent || { echo "Unsupported: no /etc/resolv.conf and no getent"; exit 3; }
echo "resolv.conf: $(readlink -f /etc/resolv.conf 2>/dev/null)"
grep -E '^(nameserver|search|domain|options)' /etc/resolv.conf 2>/dev/null | sed 's/^/  /'
if [ -d /run/systemd/system ] && have resolvectl && systemctl is-active systemd-resolved >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "systemd-resolved:"
  resolvectl status 2>/dev/null | grep -E 'Link |Current DNS|DNS Servers|DNS Domain|DNSSEC setting|Protocols' | cut -c1-120 | sed 's/^/  /'
fi
echo "nsswitch hosts: $(sed -n 's/^hosts:[[:space:]]*//p' /etc/nsswitch.conf 2>/dev/null)"

look() {
  if have getent; then getent ahosts "$1" 2>/dev/null | awk '{print $1}' | sort -u | tr '\n' ' '
  elif have nslookup; then nslookup "$1" 2>/dev/null | awk '/^Address/ && !/#/ {print $NF}' | tr '\n' ' '
  elif have host; then host "$1" 2>/dev/null | awk '/has address/ {print $NF}' | tr '\n' ' '; fi
}
rc=0
for n in localhost "$(hostname 2>/dev/null)" example.com; do
  [ -n "$n" ] || continue
  a=$(look "$n")
  if [ -n "$a" ]; then echo "lookup $n: $a"; else echo "lookup $n: FAILED"; [ "$n" = example.com ] && rc=1; fi
done
exit $rc

fields.name: Interfaces and routes report
fields.description: Lists interfaces with state, MTU, MAC and addresses plus IPv4 and IPv6 routes. Read only.
fields.script_body:
#!/bin/sh
# Lists network interfaces with state, MAC and addresses, plus the IPv4 and IPv6 routing tables.
# Variables: none
# Exit: 0 report printed, 3 no tool or /proc data to read interfaces
PATH=/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin
export PATH LC_ALL=C
set -u
command -v awk >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "awk is not installed (install gawk or mawk)"; exit 3; }

if command -v ip >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "Interfaces:"
  ip -o link show 2>/dev/null | awk '{mac = ""; for (i = 1; i <= NF; i++) { if ($i == "link/ether") mac = $(i + 1); if ($i == "mtu") mtu = $(i + 1); if ($i == "state") st = $(i + 1) } printf "  %-14s %-8s mtu %-6s %s\n", $2, st, mtu, mac}'
  echo "Addresses:"
  ip -o addr show 2>/dev/null | awk '$3 ~ /^inet/ {print "  " $2 " " $3 " " $4}'
  echo "IPv4 routes:"
  ip -4 route show 2>/dev/null | sed 's/^/  /'
  echo "IPv6 routes:"
  ip -6 route show 2>/dev/null | sed 's/^/  /'
elif command -v ifconfig >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "Interfaces:"
  ifconfig -a 2>/dev/null | sed 's/^/  /'
  echo "Routes:"
  { route -n 2>/dev/null || netstat -rn 2>/dev/null; } | sed 's/^/  /'
elif [ -r /proc/net/dev ]; then
  echo "Interfaces (no ip or ifconfig installed, names only):"
  awk 'NR > 2 {sub(":", "", $1); print "  " $1}' /proc/net/dev
  echo "IPv4 routes (hex):"
  awk 'NR > 1 {print "  " $1 " dest " $2 " gw " $3}' /proc/net/route
else
  echo "Unsupported: no ip, ifconfig or /proc/net"
  exit 3
fi

fields.name: Restart or shut down
fields.description: Schedules a restart or shutdown after a delay, or cancels a scheduled one. Logged-in users get the message.
fields.script_body:
#!/bin/sh
# Schedules a restart or shutdown, or cancels a scheduled one.
# Variables: MODE (restart, shutdown, cancel; default restart), DELAY_MINUTES (default 1, 1-1440), MESSAGE (optional notice for logged-in users).
# Exit codes: 0 scheduled or cancelled, 1 failed, 3 bad input or no shutdown command.
PATH=/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin
export PATH
set -u

mode=${MODE:-restart}
delay=${DELAY_MINUTES:-1}
msg=${MESSAGE:-}
case $mode in restart | shutdown | cancel) ;; *) echo "MODE must be restart, shutdown or cancel"; exit 3 ;; esac
case $delay in '' | *[!0-9]*) echo "DELAY_MINUTES must be a whole number"; exit 3 ;; esac
[ ${#delay} -le 4 ] && [ "$delay" -ge 1 ] && [ "$delay" -le 1440 ] || { echo "DELAY_MINUTES must be 1-1440"; exit 3; }
# a leading dash would be parsed as an option (-k only warns, -c cancels)
msg=$(printf '%s' "$msg" | tr -d '\000-\037\177' | sed 's/^[-[:space:]]*//' | cut -c1-200)
command -v shutdown >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "shutdown command not found"; exit 3; }
if [ -f /.dockerenv ] && [ ! -d /run/systemd/system ]; then
  echo "Container without init, nothing to restart"
  exit 3
fi

if [ "$mode" = cancel ]; then
  if shutdown -c >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    echo "Scheduled shutdown cancelled (or none was pending)"
    exit 0
  fi
  echo "Could not cancel"
  exit 1
fi
[ "$mode" = restart ] && flag=-r || flag=-h
if [ -n "$msg" ]; then
  shutdown "$flag" "+$delay" "$msg" >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "shutdown failed"; exit 1; }
else
  shutdown "$flag" "+$delay" >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "shutdown failed"; exit 1; }
fi
echo "$mode scheduled in $delay minute(s)"
exit 0

variables.help: Optional notice for logged-in users.
variables.name: MESSAGE
variables.label: Message

fields.name: Wake-on-LAN
fields.description: Shows or enables magic packet wake on a wired interface and makes it persistent through NetworkManager or systemd-networkd; says so when it cannot be persistent (for example under netplan). Exit 3 without hardware support.
fields.script_body:
#!/bin/sh
# Shows or enables Wake-on-LAN (magic packet) on a network interface and makes it persistent when NetworkManager or systemd-networkd manages it.
# Variables: ACTION (status, enable; default status), INTERFACE (optional, default: first physical interface).
# Exit codes: 0 ok, 1 failed or WoL still off, 3 bad input, no hardware interface or no ethtool.
PATH=/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin
export PATH
set -u

command -v awk >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "awk not found: install gawk"; exit 3; }

act=${ACTION:-status}
ifc=${INTERFACE:-}
case $act in status | enable) ;; *) echo "ACTION must be status or enable"; exit 3 ;; esac
command -v ethtool >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "ethtool not found: install the ethtool package"; exit 3; }
if [ -n "$ifc" ]; then
  case $ifc in -* | *[!A-Za-z0-9_.:-]*) echo "INTERFACE has characters that are not allowed"; exit 3 ;; esac
  [ ${#ifc} -le 15 ] || { echo "INTERFACE is too long"; exit 3; }
else
  for p in /sys/class/net/*; do
    [ -e "$p/device" ] && [ ! -e "$p/wireless" ] && ifc=${p##*/} && break
  done
  [ -n "$ifc" ] || { echo "No physical wired network interface found (virtual machine or container)"; exit 3; }
fi
[ -d "/sys/class/net/$ifc" ] || { echo "Interface $ifc does not exist"; exit 3; }

wol() { ethtool "$ifc" 2>/dev/null | awk -F': ' '/^[ \t]*Wake-on:/ {print $2}'; }
sup=$(ethtool "$ifc" 2>/dev/null | awk -F': ' '/Supports Wake-on:/ {print $2}')
case $sup in *g*) ;; *) echo "$ifc does not support magic packet wake (supports: ${sup:-none})"; exit 3 ;; esac
cur=$(wol)
if [ "$act" = status ]; then
  echo "$ifc Wake-on: $cur"
  case $cur in *g*) exit 0 ;; *) exit 1 ;; esac
fi

changed=
case $cur in *g*) ;; *) ethtool -s "$ifc" wol g >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "ethtool could not enable WoL on $ifc"; exit 1; }; changed=1 ;; esac
cur=$(wol)
case $cur in *g*) ;; *) echo "$ifc still reports Wake-on: $cur"; exit 1 ;; esac

how=
if command -v nmcli >/dev/null 2>&1 && nmcli -t -f DEVICE,STATE device 2>/dev/null | grep -q "^$ifc:"; then
  con=$(nmcli -t -g GENERAL.CONNECTION device show "$ifc" 2>/dev/null)
  if [ -n "$con" ] && nmcli connection modify "$con" 802-3-ethernet.wake-on-lan magic >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    how="NetworkManager profile $con"
  fi
fi
# only the first matching .link file applies, and netplan generates 10-netplan-*.link
if [ -z "$how" ] && command -v netplan >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "$ifc Wake-on: $cur${changed:+ (enabled now)}; not persistent: netplan manages $ifc, add wakeonlan: true to it in /etc/netplan and run netplan apply"
  exit 0
fi
if [ -z "$how" ] && [ -d /run/systemd/system ] && command -v networkctl >/dev/null 2>&1 &&
  networkctl list 2>/dev/null | grep -qw "$ifc"; then
  f=/etc/systemd/network/50-ulrmm-wol-$ifc.link
  printf '[Match]\nOriginalName=%s\n\n[Link]\nWakeOnLan=magic\n' "$ifc" >"$f" && how="systemd-networkd link file $f"
fi
if [ -n "$how" ]; then
  echo "$ifc Wake-on: $cur, persistent via $how${changed:+ (enabled now)}"
else
  echo "$ifc Wake-on: $cur${changed:+ (enabled now)}; not persistent: neither NetworkManager nor systemd-networkd manages $ifc, it resets at reboot"
fi
exit 0

variables.help: Optional, default is the first physical wired interface.
variables.name: INTERFACE
variables.label: Interface

fields.name: SSH server
fields.description: Installs the OpenSSH server if missing, enables and starts it, and can open its port in ufw or firewalld.
fields.script_body:
#!/bin/sh
# Installs OpenSSH server if missing, enables and starts it, and optionally opens the port in ufw or firewalld.
# Variables: OPEN_FIREWALL (default false).
# Exit codes: 0 sshd running, 1 failed, 3 bad input or unsupported system.
PATH=/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin
export PATH
set -u

command -v awk >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "awk not found: install gawk"; exit 3; }

fw=${OPEN_FIREWALL:-false}
case $fw in true | false) ;; *) echo "OPEN_FIREWALL must be true or false"; exit 3 ;; esac
did=
if ! command -v sshd >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  export DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive
  if command -v apt-get >/dev/null 2>&1; then apt-get update >/dev/null 2>&1; apt-get install -y openssh-server >/dev/null 2>&1
  elif command -v dnf >/dev/null 2>&1; then dnf -y install openssh-server >/dev/null 2>&1
  elif command -v yum >/dev/null 2>&1; then yum -y install openssh-server >/dev/null 2>&1
  elif command -v zypper >/dev/null 2>&1; then zypper -n install openssh-server >/dev/null 2>&1 || zypper -n install openssh >/dev/null 2>&1
  elif command -v pacman >/dev/null 2>&1; then pacman -S --needed --noconfirm openssh >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "pacman could not install openssh; if the package databases are stale, run a full upgrade (pacman -Syu) first"; exit 1; }
  elif command -v apk >/dev/null 2>&1; then apk add openssh-server >/dev/null 2>&1
  else echo "No supported package manager found"; exit 3; fi
  command -v sshd >/dev/null 2>&1 || [ -x /usr/sbin/sshd ] || { echo "Installing the OpenSSH server failed"; exit 1; }
  did="installed"
fi
if ! ls /etc/ssh/ssh_host_*_key >/dev/null 2>&1; then ssh-keygen -A >/dev/null 2>&1; fi
mkdir -p /run/sshd 2>/dev/null
if [ -d /run/systemd/system ]; then
  unit=sshd
  systemctl cat ssh >/dev/null 2>&1 && unit=ssh
  systemctl cat "$unit" >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "No ssh or sshd unit found"; exit 1; }
  systemctl enable "$unit" >/dev/null 2>&1
  systemctl is-active "$unit" >/dev/null 2>&1 || { systemctl start "$unit" >/dev/null 2>&1 && did="${did:+$did, }started"; }
  systemctl is-active "$unit" >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "$unit is not running"; exit 1; }
elif command -v rc-service >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  rc-update add sshd default >/dev/null 2>&1
  rc-service sshd status >/dev/null 2>&1 || { rc-service sshd start >/dev/null 2>&1 && did="${did:+$did, }started"; }
  rc-service sshd status >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "sshd is not running"; exit 1; }
else
  echo "Neither systemd nor OpenRC found"
  exit 3
fi
port=$(sshd -T 2>/dev/null | awk '$1=="port" {print $2; exit}')
port=${port:-22}
if [ "$fw" = true ]; then
  fwd=
  command -v firewall-cmd >/dev/null 2>&1 && [ "$(firewall-cmd --state 2>/dev/null)" = running ] && fwd=1
  if command -v ufw >/dev/null 2>&1 && { [ -z "$fwd" ] || ufw status 2>/dev/null | grep -q '^Status: active'; }; then
    ufw allow "$port/tcp" >/dev/null 2>&1 && did="${did:+$did, }ufw port $port open"
  elif [ -n "$fwd" ]; then
    firewall-cmd --permanent --add-port="$port/tcp" >/dev/null 2>&1
    firewall-cmd --add-port="$port/tcp" >/dev/null 2>&1 && did="${did:+$did, }firewalld port $port open"
  else
    echo "Note: no active ufw or firewalld found, no firewall rule added"
  fi
fi
echo "SSH server running on port $port${did:+ ($did)}"
exit 0

variables.name: OPEN_FIREWALL
variables.label: Open firewall

fields.name: fail2ban status report
fields.description: Reports whether fail2ban runs, its jails and the banned addresses. Exit 1 when installed but stopped, 3 when not installed.
fields.script_body:
#!/bin/sh
# Reports fail2ban state, its jails and the currently banned addresses per jail.
# Variables: none. Exit codes: 0 running, 1 installed but not running, 3 fail2ban not installed.
PATH=/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin
export PATH
set -u

command -v fail2ban-client >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "fail2ban is not installed (package fail2ban)"; exit 3; }
if ! fail2ban-client ping >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "fail2ban is installed but not running"
  exit 1
fi
jails=$(fail2ban-client status 2>/dev/null | sed -n 's/.*Jail list:[[:space:]]*//p' | tr -d ',')
n=0
for j in $jails; do n=$((n + 1)); done
echo "fail2ban running, $n jail(s)"
for j in $jails; do
  case $j in *[!A-Za-z0-9_.-]* | -*) continue ;; esac
  s=$(fail2ban-client status "$j" 2>/dev/null)
  cur=$(printf '%s\n' "$s" | sed -n 's/.*Currently banned:[[:space:]]*//p')
  tot=$(printf '%s\n' "$s" | sed -n 's/.*Total banned:[[:space:]]*//p')
  ips=$(printf '%s\n' "$s" | sed -n 's/.*Banned IP list:[[:space:]]*//p' | cut -c1-300)
  echo "$j: banned now $cur, total $tot${ips:+, $ips}"
done
exit 0

fields.name: Firewall port
fields.description: Opens, blocks or removes a firewall rule for one TCP or UDP port with ufw or firewalld (the active one first); refuses to block any SSH port. Exit 3 with any other firewall.
fields.script_body:
#!/bin/sh
# Opens, blocks or removes a firewall rule for one TCP or UDP port with ufw or firewalld.
# Variables: ACTION (allow, deny, remove; default allow), PORT (required, 1-65535), PROTOCOL (tcp, udp; default tcp).
# Exit codes: 0 rule in place, 1 failed, 3 bad input, no ufw or firewalld, or the rule would block SSH.
PATH=/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin
export PATH
set -u

command -v awk >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "awk not found: install gawk"; exit 3; }

act=${ACTION:-allow}
port=${PORT:-}
proto=${PROTOCOL:-tcp}
case $act in allow | deny | remove) ;; *) echo "ACTION must be allow, deny or remove"; exit 3 ;; esac
case $proto in tcp | udp) ;; *) echo "PROTOCOL must be tcp or udp"; exit 3 ;; esac
case $port in '' | *[!0-9]*) echo "PORT must be a whole number"; exit 3 ;; esac
[ ${#port} -le 5 ] && [ "$port" -ge 1 ] && [ "$port" -le 65535 ] || { echo "PORT must be 1-65535"; exit 3; }
port=$((port + 0))

if [ "$act" != allow ]; then
  sshp=
  if command -v sshd >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    mkdir -p /run/sshd 2>/dev/null
    sshp=$(sshd -T 2>/dev/null | awk '$1=="port" {print $2} $1=="listenaddress" {n = split($2, a, ":"); print a[n]}')
  fi
  if [ "$proto" = tcp ] && printf '%s\n' 22 "$sshp" | grep -qx "$port"; then
    echo "Refusing to $act port $port/tcp: it is the SSH port"
    exit 3
  fi
fi

# the active firewall gets the rule; an installed but inactive ufw only when firewalld is not running
fwd=
command -v firewall-cmd >/dev/null 2>&1 && [ "$(firewall-cmd --state 2>/dev/null)" = running ] && fwd=1
if command -v ufw >/dev/null 2>&1 && { [ -z "$fwd" ] || ufw status 2>/dev/null | grep -q '^Status: active'; }; then
  r="$port/$proto"
  case $act in
  allow) ufw allow "$r" >/dev/null 2>&1 ;;
  deny) ufw deny "$r" >/dev/null 2>&1 ;;
  remove)
    ufw delete allow "$r" >/dev/null 2>&1
    ufw delete deny "$r" >/dev/null 2>&1
    ;;
  esac
  rules=$(ufw show added 2>/dev/null | grep -E "^ufw (allow|deny) $r\$")
  case $act in
  allow | deny) printf '%s\n' "$rules" | grep -qx "ufw $act $r" || { echo "ufw rule not present after change"; exit 1; } ;;
  remove) [ -z "$rules" ] || { echo "ufw rule still present"; exit 1; } ;;
  esac
  ufw status 2>/dev/null | grep -q '^Status: active' || echo "Note: ufw is not active, the rule applies once it is enabled"
  echo "ufw: $act $r done"
  exit 0
fi
if command -v firewall-cmd >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  [ "$(firewall-cmd --state 2>/dev/null)" = running ] || { echo "firewalld is installed but not running"; exit 3; }
  r="$port/$proto"
  rich="rule port port=$port protocol=$proto reject"
  for perm in --permanent ""; do
    case $act in
    allow)
      firewall-cmd $perm --remove-rich-rule="$rich" >/dev/null 2>&1
      firewall-cmd $perm --add-port="$r" >/dev/null 2>&1
      ;;
    deny)
      firewall-cmd $perm --remove-port="$r" >/dev/null 2>&1
      firewall-cmd $perm --add-rich-rule="$rich" >/dev/null 2>&1
      ;;
    remove)
      firewall-cmd $perm --remove-port="$r" >/dev/null 2>&1
      firewall-cmd $perm --remove-rich-rule="$rich" >/dev/null 2>&1
      ;;
    esac
  done
  open=$(firewall-cmd --permanent --query-port="$r" 2>/dev/null)
  blk=$(firewall-cmd --permanent --query-rich-rule="$rich" 2>/dev/null)
  case $act in
  allow) [ "$open" = yes ] || { echo "firewalld port not open after change"; exit 1; } ;;
  deny) [ "$blk" = yes ] || { echo "firewalld reject rule missing after change"; exit 1; } ;;
  remove) [ "$open" = no ] && [ "$blk" = no ] || { echo "firewalld rule still present"; exit 1; } ;;
  esac
  echo "firewalld: $act $r done (runtime and permanent)"
  exit 0
fi
echo "Neither ufw nor firewalld is installed; port rules are only supported for those"
exit 3

fields.name: Firewall status check
fields.description: Reports which firewall is active (ufw, firewalld, nftables, iptables), its default policy and open ports. Exit 1 when nothing filters, 3 when no firewall tool is installed.
fields.script_body:
#!/bin/sh
# Reports which host firewall is active (ufw, firewalld, nftables, iptables), its default policy and open ports.
# Variables: none. Exit codes: 0 a firewall filters, 1 nothing filters, 3 no firewall tool installed.
PATH=/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin
export PATH
set -u

command -v awk >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "awk not found: install gawk"; exit 3; }

active=
detail=
found=
if command -v ufw >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  found=1
  s=$(ufw status verbose 2>/dev/null)
  case $s in
  *"Status: active"*)
    active="$active ufw"
    detail="$detail
ufw: $(printf '%s\n' "$s" | grep '^Default:')
ufw rules: $(printf '%s\n' "$s" | awk '/ALLOW|DENY|REJECT|LIMIT/ && !/\(v6\)/ {printf "%s %s; ", $1, $(NF-1)" "$NF}' | cut -c1-600)"
    ;;
  esac
fi
if command -v firewall-cmd >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  found=1
  if [ "$(firewall-cmd --state 2>/dev/null)" = running ]; then
    active="$active firewalld"
    z=$(firewall-cmd --get-default-zone 2>/dev/null)
    detail="$detail
firewalld: default zone $z, services: $(firewall-cmd --list-services 2>/dev/null), ports: $(firewall-cmd --list-ports 2>/dev/null)"
  fi
fi
if command -v nft >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  found=1
  n=$(nft list ruleset 2>/dev/null)
  # only input chains count: container runtimes add forward chains with a drop policy on their own
  if printf '%s\n' "$n" | awk '/^[[:space:]]*chain / {c = 0} /hook input/ {c = 1; if (/policy drop/) a = 1; next} c && /(drop|reject)/ {a = 1} END {exit !a}'; then
    pol=$(printf '%s\n' "$n" | grep -Eo 'hook input[^;]*; (policy [a-z]+)?' | head -1)
    if ! printf '%s\n' "$active" | grep -Eq 'ufw|firewalld'; then
      active="$active nftables"
      detail="$detail
nftables: $pol, ports: $(printf '%s\n' "$n" | grep -Eo '(tcp|udp) dport [{ 0-9,a-z-]+' | tr '\n' ';' | cut -c1-400)"
    fi
  fi
fi
if command -v iptables >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  found=1
  i=$(iptables -S 2>/dev/null)
  if printf '%s\n' "$i" | grep -Eq '^-P INPUT (DROP|REJECT)|^-A INPUT .*-j (DROP|REJECT)'; then
    case $active in *ufw* | *firewalld* | *nftables*) ;; *)
      active="$active iptables"
      detail="$detail
iptables: $(printf '%s\n' "$i" | grep '^-P INPUT'), ports: $(printf '%s\n' "$i" | grep -Eo -e '-p (tcp|udp).*--dport [0-9:]+' | tr '\n' ';' | cut -c1-400)"
      ;;
    esac
  fi
fi
if [ -z "$found" ]; then
  echo "No firewall tool installed (ufw, firewalld, nft, iptables)"
  exit 3
fi
if [ -z "$active" ]; then
  echo "No active firewall: nothing filters inbound traffic"
  exit 1
fi
echo "Firewall active:$active"
printf '%s\n' "$detail" | sed '/^$/d'
exit 0

fields.name: Mandatory access control report
fields.description: Reports the SELinux and AppArmor state. Exit 2 when none of them is enforcing.
fields.script_body:
#!/bin/sh
# Reports the SELinux and AppArmor state.
# Variables: none. Exit codes: 0 one of them enforcing, 2 none enforcing (disabled, permissive or absent).
PATH=/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin
export PATH
set -u

enf=
se=absent
if command -v getenforce >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  se=$(getenforce 2>/dev/null)
elif [ -r /sys/fs/selinux/enforce ]; then
  case $(cat /sys/fs/selinux/enforce) in 1) se=Enforcing ;; *) se=Permissive ;; esac
fi
[ "$se" = Enforcing ] && enf=1
aa=absent
if [ -r /sys/module/apparmor/parameters/enabled ] && [ "$(cat /sys/module/apparmor/parameters/enabled)" = Y ]; then
  prof=/sys/kernel/security/apparmor/profiles
  if [ -r "$prof" ]; then
    total=$(wc -l <"$prof")
    encl=$(grep -c '(enforce)' "$prof")
    aa="enabled, $total profile(s), $encl enforcing"
    [ "$encl" -gt 0 ] && enf=1
  else
    aa="enabled in kernel, profiles not readable"
  fi
elif command -v aa-status >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  aa="tools installed, kernel module off"
fi
echo "SELinux: $se"
echo "AppArmor: $aa"
if [ -n "$enf" ]; then
  echo "Mandatory access control is enforcing"
  exit 0
fi
echo "No mandatory access control is enforcing"
exit 2

fields.name: Privileged access audit
fields.description: Lists uid 0 accounts, sudo and wheel members, NOPASSWD rules and accounts with an empty password. Exit 1 on an empty password or an extra uid 0 account.
fields.script_body:
#!/bin/sh
# Lists uid 0 accounts, sudo/wheel/admin members, NOPASSWD sudo rules and accounts with an empty password.
# Variables: none. Exit codes: 0 clean, 1 empty password or an extra uid 0 account, 3 /etc/passwd unreadable.
PATH=/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin
export PATH
set -u

command -v awk >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "awk not found: install gawk"; exit 3; }

[ -r /etc/passwd ] || { echo "/etc/passwd not readable"; exit 3; }
bad=
uid0=$(awk -F: '$3==0 {print $1}' /etc/passwd | tr '\n' ' ')
extra=$(awk -F: '$3==0 && $1!="root" {print $1}' /etc/passwd | tr '\n' ' ')
[ -n "$extra" ] && bad=1
empty=
if [ -r /etc/shadow ]; then
  empty=$(awk -F: '$2=="" {print $1}' /etc/shadow | tr '\n' ' ')
  [ -n "$empty" ] && bad=1
fi
admins=
for g in sudo wheel admin; do
  m=$(getent group "$g" 2>/dev/null | cut -d: -f4 | tr ',' ' ')
  [ -n "$m" ] && admins="$admins $g:[$m]"
done
nopw=$( { cat /etc/sudoers; find /etc/sudoers.d -type f 2>/dev/null | while read -r f; do cat "$f"; done; } 2>/dev/null |
  grep -E '^[^#]*NOPASSWD' | sed 's/[[:space:]]\+/ /g' | cut -c1-120)

if [ -n "$bad" ]; then echo "Privileged access audit: problems found"; else echo "Privileged access audit: no problems"; fi
echo "uid 0 accounts: ${uid0:-none}"
[ -n "$extra" ] && echo "EXTRA uid 0 accounts: $extra"
echo "admin group members:${admins:- none}"
echo "empty password accounts: ${empty:-none}"
if [ -n "$nopw" ]; then
  echo "NOPASSWD sudo rules:"
  printf '%s\n' "$nopw"
else
  echo "NOPASSWD sudo rules: none"
fi
[ -z "$bad" ]

fields.name: SSH configuration audit
fields.description: Checks the effective sshd settings for weak options (root login, password login, empty passwords, weak ciphers and MACs). Exit 2 when weak settings are found.
fields.script_body:
#!/bin/sh
# Audits the effective sshd settings (sshd -T) for weak configuration.
# Variables: none. Exit codes: 0 no findings, 2 weak settings found, 3 sshd not installed or not readable.
PATH=/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin
export PATH
set -u

command -v awk >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "awk not found: install gawk"; exit 3; }

command -v sshd >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "sshd is not installed"; exit 3; }
tmp=$(mktemp -d) || exit 3
trap 'rm -rf "$tmp"' EXIT
cfg=
[ -f /etc/ssh/sshd_config ] && cfg="-f /etc/ssh/sshd_config"
# shellcheck disable=SC2086
if ! sshd -T $cfg >"$tmp/t" 2>/dev/null; then
  command -v ssh-keygen >/dev/null 2>&1 && ssh-keygen -q -t ed25519 -N '' -f "$tmp/k" >/dev/null 2>&1
  # shellcheck disable=SC2086
  sshd -T $cfg -h "$tmp/k" >"$tmp/t" 2>"$tmp/e" || { echo "sshd -T failed: $(head -1 "$tmp/e")"; exit 3; }
fi
g() { awk -v k="$1" '$1==k {sub(/^[^ ]+ /,""); print; exit}' "$tmp/t"; }
find=
add() { find="$find
- $*"; }

[ "$(g permitrootlogin)" = yes ] && add "root login with password is allowed (PermitRootLogin yes)"
[ "$(g passwordauthentication)" = yes ] && add "password authentication is on"
[ "$(g permitemptypasswords)" = yes ] && add "empty passwords are allowed"
[ "$(g hostbasedauthentication)" = yes ] && add "host-based authentication is on"
[ "$(g permituserenvironment)" = yes ] && add "PermitUserEnvironment is on"
[ "$(g ignorerhosts)" = no ] && add "rhosts files are honoured"
[ "$(g pubkeyauthentication)" = no ] && add "public key authentication is off"
m=$(g maxauthtries)
[ -n "$m" ] && [ "$m" -gt 6 ] 2>/dev/null && add "MaxAuthTries is $m"
[ "$(g protocol)" = 1 ] && add "protocol 1 is enabled"
g ciphers | tr ',' '\n' | grep -Eq '3des|arcfour|blowfish|cast128|-cbc' && add "weak ciphers are offered (CBC, 3DES or RC4)"
g macs | tr ',' '\n' | grep -Eq '^hmac-md5|-96$' && add "weak MACs are offered (MD5 or 96-bit)"
g kexalgorithms | tr ',' '\n' | grep -Eq 'diffie-hellman-group1-|diffie-hellman-group-exchange-sha1' && add "weak key exchange is offered (SHA1 or group1)"

echo "port $(g port), root login $(g permitrootlogin), password auth $(g passwordauthentication), empty passwords $(g permitemptypasswords)"
if [ -n "$find" ]; then
  echo "SSH configuration has weak settings:$find"
  exit 2
fi
echo "SSH configuration looks sound"
exit 0

fields.name: SSH password authentication
fields.description: Shows, disables or enables SSH password login. Disabling is refused unless root or a sudo user has a usable authorized key; sshd -t runs first and the old config is restored on failure.
fields.script_body:
#!/bin/sh
# Shows, disables or enables SSH password login. Disabling needs a usable authorized key for root or a sudo/wheel user.
# Variables: STATE (status, disable, enable; default status).
# Exit codes: 0 ok (status: password login off), 1 failed or status shows password login on, 3 bad input, no sshd, or unsafe to disable.
PATH=/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin
export PATH
set -u

command -v awk >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "awk not found: install gawk"; exit 3; }
set -f

st=${STATE:-status}
case $st in status | disable | enable) ;; *) echo "STATE must be status, disable or enable"; exit 3 ;; esac
command -v sshd >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "sshd is not installed"; exit 3; }
main=/etc/ssh/sshd_config
[ -f "$main" ] || { echo "$main not found"; exit 3; }
tmp=$(mktemp -d) || exit 3
trap 'rm -rf "$tmp"' EXIT
if command -v ssh-keygen >/dev/null 2>&1; then ssh-keygen -q -t ed25519 -N '' -f "$tmp/k" >/dev/null 2>&1; fi
# Debian's sshd -T refuses to run while sshd is stopped and its privsep directory is gone
mkdir -p /run/sshd 2>/dev/null

conf() { sshd -T -f "$main" "$@" 2>/dev/null || sshd -T -f "$main" -h "$tmp/k" "$@" 2>/dev/null; }
eff() { conf | awk -v k="$1" '$1==k {print $2; exit}'; }
# Password login is on when PasswordAuthentication is yes or PAM answers keyboard-interactive.
pwon() { [ "$(eff passwordauthentication)" = yes ] || { [ "$(eff kbdinteractiveauthentication)" = yes ] && [ "$(eff usepam)" = yes ]; }; }
cur=$(eff passwordauthentication)
[ -n "$cur" ] || { echo "Cannot read the effective sshd configuration: $(sshd -T -f "$main" 2>&1 | head -1)"; exit 3; }
if [ "$st" = status ]; then
  echo "SSH password authentication: $cur, keyboard-interactive: $(eff kbdinteractiveauthentication), PAM: $(eff usepam)"
  pwon && exit 1 || exit 0
fi
want=yes
[ "$st" = disable ] && want=no
if { [ "$st" = enable ] && [ "$cur" = yes ]; } || { [ "$st" = disable ] && ! pwon; }; then
  echo "SSH password authentication already $want"
  exit 0
fi

# shellcheck disable=SC2254
# Succeeds when user $1 can log in with a plain key line from an authorized_keys file sshd reads for them.
keyuser() {
  ku=$1
  ent=$(getent passwd "$ku") || return 1
  case $(printf '%s' "$ent" | cut -d: -f7) in */nologin | */false | '') return 1 ;; esac
  home=$(printf '%s' "$ent" | cut -d: -f6)
  uid=$(printf '%s' "$ent" | cut -d: -f3)
  sp=$(awk -F: -v u="$ku" '$1==u' /etc/shadow 2>/dev/null)
  exp=$(printf '%s' "$sp" | cut -d: -f8)
  case $exp in '' | *[!0-9]*) ;; *) [ "$exp" -gt $(($(date +%s) / 86400)) ] || return 1 ;; esac
  case $(printf '%s' "$sp" | cut -d: -f2) in '!'*) [ "$(eff usepam)" = yes ] || return 1 ;; esac
  conf -C "user=$ku,host=localhost,addr=127.0.0.1" >"$tmp/u" || return 1
  v() { awk -v k="$1" '$1==k {sub(/^[^ ]+ /, ""); print}' "$tmp/u"; }
  [ "$(v pubkeyauthentication)" = yes ] || return 1
  if [ "$ku" = root ]; then case $(v permitrootlogin) in yes | prohibit-password | without-password) ;; *) return 1 ;; esac; fi
  am=
  for m in $(v authenticationmethods); do case $m in any | publickey) am=1 ;; esac; done
  [ -n "$am" ] || return 1
  grp=" $(id -Gn "$ku" 2>/dev/null) "
  for p in $(v denyusers); do case $p in *@*) return 1 ;; esac; case $ku in $p) return 1 ;; esac; done
  for p in $(v denygroups); do for g in $grp; do case $g in $p) return 1 ;; esac; done; done
  if [ -n "$(v allowusers)" ]; then
    hit=
    for p in $(v allowusers); do case $p in *@*) ;; *) case $ku in $p) hit=1 ;; esac ;; esac; done
    [ -n "$hit" ] || return 1
  fi
  if [ -n "$(v allowgroups)" ]; then
    hit=
    for p in $(v allowgroups); do for g in $grp; do case $g in $p) hit=1 ;; esac; done; done
    [ -n "$hit" ] || return 1
  fi
  strict=$(v strictmodes)
  for akf in $(v authorizedkeysfile); do
    [ "$akf" = none ] && continue
    f=$(awk -v p="$akf" -v h="$home" -v u="$ku" -v i="$uid" 'BEGIN {
      while ((n = index(p, "%")) > 0) { c = substr(p, n + 1, 1); o = o substr(p, 1, n - 1) (c == "h" ? h : c == "u" ? u : c == "U" ? i : c == "%" ? "%" : "%" c); p = substr(p, n + 2) }
      print o p }')
    case $f in /*) ;; *) f=$home/$f ;; esac
    [ -f "$f" ] && [ ! -L "$f" ] || continue
    grep -Eq '^(ssh-(ed25519|rsa)|ecdsa-sha2-nistp[0-9]+|sk-[a-z0-9@.-]+) ' "$f" || continue
    # StrictModes: sshd ignores the file when it or a parent is not owned by root or the user, or is group/world writable
    if [ "$strict" != no ]; then
      p=$f bad=
      while [ -n "$p" ]; do
        # shellcheck disable=SC2046
        set -- $(stat -L -c '%u %a' "$p" 2>/dev/null)
        { [ "${1:-x}" = 0 ] || [ "${1:-x}" = "$uid" ]; } && [ $((0${2:-777} & 022)) -eq 0 ] || { bad=1; break; }
        [ "$p" = / ] && break
        p=$(dirname "$p")
      done
      [ -z "$bad" ] || continue
    fi
    return 0
  done
  return 1
}

if [ "$st" = disable ]; then
  ok=
  members=
  for g in sudo wheel admin; do
    members="$members $(getent group "$g" 2>/dev/null | cut -d: -f4 | tr ',' ' ')"
  done
  for u in root $members; do
    case " $ok " in *" $u "*) continue ;; esac
    keyuser "$u" && ok="$ok $u"
  done
  if [ -z "$ok" ]; then
    echo "Refusing to disable password login: neither root nor a sudo/wheel member can log in with an authorized key"
    echo "(checked: login shell, locked or expired account, PubkeyAuthentication, PermitRootLogin, AuthenticationMethods,"
    echo " Allow/DenyUsers, Allow/DenyGroups, AuthorizedKeysFile and StrictModes ownership and modes)"
    exit 3
  fi
  echo "Key login available for:$ok"
fi

reload() {
  if [ -d /run/systemd/system ]; then
    systemctl reload ssh >/dev/null 2>&1 || systemctl reload sshd >/dev/null 2>&1 || systemctl restart sshd >/dev/null 2>&1 || systemctl restart ssh >/dev/null 2>&1
  elif command -v rc-service >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    rc-service sshd reload >/dev/null 2>&1
  else
    # only the listener: per-connection sshd processes die on SIGHUP
    pf=$(eff pidfile)
    [ -s "$pf" ] && kill -HUP "$(cat "$pf")" 2>/dev/null
  fi
}
done_ok() { [ "$(eff passwordauthentication)" = "$want" ] && { [ "$st" = enable ] || ! pwon; }; }
chk() { sshd -t -f "$main" 2>"$tmp/e" || sshd -t -f "$main" -h "$tmp/k" 2>"$tmp/e"; }
running() { pgrep -x sshd >/dev/null 2>&1; }

dropin=/etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/00-ulrmm-password-auth.conf
write_dropin() {
  printf 'PasswordAuthentication %s\n' "$want" >"$dropin"
  if [ "$st" = disable ] && [ -n "$(eff kbdinteractiveauthentication)" ]; then
    printf 'KbdInteractiveAuthentication no\n' >>"$dropin"
  fi
}
used=
if grep -Eq '^[[:space:]]*Include[[:space:]]+/etc/ssh/sshd_config\.d/' "$main" && [ -d /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d ]; then
  prev=
  [ -f "$dropin" ] && cp -p "$dropin" "$tmp/dropin.bak" && prev=1
  write_dropin
  if chk && done_ok; then
    used="drop-in $dropin"
  else
    if [ -n "$prev" ]; then cp -p "$tmp/dropin.bak" "$dropin"; else rm -f "$dropin"; fi
  fi
fi
if [ -z "$used" ]; then
  cp -p "$main" "$tmp/main.bak" || exit 1
  [ -f "$main.ulrmm.bak" ] || cp -p "$main" "$main.ulrmm.bak"
  {
    printf 'PasswordAuthentication %s\n' "$want"
    [ "$st" = disable ] && [ -n "$(eff kbdinteractiveauthentication)" ] && printf 'KbdInteractiveAuthentication no\n'
    awk -v st="$st" 'tolower($1) == "match" {m = 1} !m && (tolower($1) == "passwordauthentication" || st == "disable" && tolower($1) == "kbdinteractiveauthentication") {$0 = "#" $0} {print}' "$main"
  } >"$tmp/new"
  # replace by rename so a killed run never leaves a truncated sshd_config
  put() { cp -p "$main" "$main.ulrmm.new" && cat "$1" >"$main.ulrmm.new" && mv -f "$main.ulrmm.new" "$main"; }
  put "$tmp/new" || { rm -f "$main.ulrmm.new"; echo "Writing $main failed"; exit 1; }
  if chk && done_ok; then
    used="$main (backup $main.ulrmm.bak)"
  else
    put "$tmp/main.bak"
    echo "sshd rejected the change, original restored: $(head -1 "$tmp/e")"
    exit 1
  fi
fi
if running; then
  reload || { echo "SSH password authentication set to $want via $used, but reloading sshd failed: restart it"; exit 1; }
  sleep 1
  running || { echo "sshd is not running after reload"; exit 1; }
  echo "SSH password authentication set to $want via $used, sshd reloaded"
else
  echo "SSH password authentication set to $want via $used (sshd not running, applied on next start)"
fi
if [ "$st" = disable ] && awk 'FNR == 1 {m = 0} tolower($1) == "match" {m = 1} m && tolower($1) ~ /^(passwordauthentication|kbdinteractiveauthentication)$/ && tolower($2) == "yes" {f = 1} END {exit !f}' "$main" /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/*.conf 2>/dev/null; then
  echo "Note: a Match block still allows passwords for some users or addresses"
fi
exit 0

fields.name: Install packages
fields.description: Installs packages non-interactively with the detected package manager (apt, dnf, yum, zypper, pacman, apk) after refreshing metadata, or reports whether they are installed. Verifies the result.
fields.script_body:
#!/bin/sh
# Installs packages with the system package manager (apt, dnf, yum, zypper, pacman, apk) or reports whether they are installed.
# Variables: PACKAGES (required, names separated by spaces, commas or line breaks), ACTION (install, status; default install).
# Exit codes: 0 all installed, 1 install failed or a package is missing, 3 bad input or no package manager.
PATH=/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin
export PATH
set -u

set -f
act=${ACTION:-install}
list=$(printf '%s' "${PACKAGES:-}" | tr ',\r\n\t' '    ')
case $act in install | status) ;; *) echo "ACTION must be install or status"; exit 3 ;; esac
n=0
for p in $list; do
  case $p in -* | *[!A-Za-z0-9+._:@-]*) echo "Package name '$p' has characters that are not allowed"; exit 3 ;; esac
  [ ${#p} -le 100 ] || { echo "Package name too long"; exit 3; }
  n=$((n + 1))
done
[ "$n" -ge 1 ] && [ "$n" -le 50 ] || { echo "PACKAGES needs 1-50 package names"; exit 3; }
for c in apt-get dnf yum zypper pacman apk; do
  command -v "$c" >/dev/null 2>&1 && pm=$c && break
done
[ -n "${pm:-}" ] || { echo "No supported package manager found"; exit 3; }

have() {
  case $pm in
  apt-get) dpkg -s "$1" 2>/dev/null | grep -q '^Status: install ok installed' ;;
  dnf | yum | zypper) rpm -q "$1" >/dev/null 2>&1 || rpm -q --whatprovides "$1" >/dev/null 2>&1 ;;
  pacman) pacman -Qq "$1" >/dev/null 2>&1 ;;
  apk) apk info -e "$1" >/dev/null 2>&1 ;;
  esac
}
missing=
for p in $list; do have "$p" || missing="$missing $p"; done
if [ "$act" = status ]; then
  for p in $list; do if have "$p"; then echo "$p: installed"; else echo "$p: missing"; fi; done
  [ -z "$missing" ]
  exit $?
fi
if [ -z "$missing" ]; then
  echo "Already installed: $list"
  exit 0
fi
export DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive
# shellcheck disable=SC2086
case $pm in
apt-get)
  apt-get -o DPkg::Lock::Timeout=300 update >/dev/null 2>&1
  apt-get install -y -o DPkg::Lock::Timeout=300 -o Dpkg::Options::=--force-confold $missing >/dev/null 2>&1
  ;;
dnf | yum)
  $pm -y makecache >/dev/null 2>&1
  $pm -y install $missing >/dev/null 2>&1
  ;;
zypper)
  zypper -n refresh >/dev/null 2>&1
  zypper -n install --no-recommends $missing >/dev/null 2>&1
  ;;
pacman)
  # no -Sy here: refreshing the databases without a full upgrade is an unsupported partial upgrade
  pacman -S --needed --noconfirm $missing >/dev/null 2>&1 || echo "pacman failed; if the package databases are stale, run a full upgrade (pacman -Syu) first"
  ;;
apk)
  apk update >/dev/null 2>&1
  apk add $missing >/dev/null 2>&1
  ;;
esac
rc=$?
bad=
for p in $missing; do have "$p" || bad="$bad $p"; done
if [ -n "$bad" ]; then
  echo "Not installed after $pm (exit $rc):$bad"
  exit 1
fi
echo "Installed with $pm:$missing"
exit 0

variables.help: Package names separated by spaces or commas.
variables.name: PACKAGES
variables.label: Packages

fields.name: QEMU guest agent
fields.description: Installs and starts the QEMU guest agent on a KVM/QEMU virtual machine. Exit 3 on physical hosts, containers and other hypervisors.
fields.script_body:
#!/bin/sh
# Installs and starts the QEMU guest agent on a KVM/QEMU virtual machine.
# Variables: none. Exit codes: 0 agent running, 1 install or start failed, 3 not a QEMU/KVM guest or unsupported system.
PATH=/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin
export PATH
set -u

if [ -f /.dockerenv ] || grep -qaE 'docker|lxc|containerd|kubepods' /proc/1/cgroup 2>/dev/null; then
  echo "This is a container, not a virtual machine"
  exit 3
fi
vm=
if command -v systemd-detect-virt >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  case $(systemd-detect-virt 2>/dev/null) in kvm | qemu) vm=1 ;; esac
fi
grep -qiE 'qemu|kvm' /sys/class/dmi/id/sys_vendor /sys/class/dmi/id/product_name 2>/dev/null && vm=1
[ -e /dev/virtio-ports/org.qemu.guest_agent.0 ] && vm=1
[ -n "$vm" ] || { echo "This is not a QEMU/KVM guest"; exit 3; }

if ! command -v qemu-ga >/dev/null 2>&1 && [ ! -x /usr/sbin/qemu-ga ]; then
  export DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive
  if command -v apt-get >/dev/null 2>&1; then apt-get update >/dev/null 2>&1; apt-get install -y qemu-guest-agent >/dev/null 2>&1
  elif command -v dnf >/dev/null 2>&1; then dnf -y install qemu-guest-agent >/dev/null 2>&1
  elif command -v yum >/dev/null 2>&1; then yum -y install qemu-guest-agent >/dev/null 2>&1
  elif command -v zypper >/dev/null 2>&1; then zypper -n install qemu-guest-agent >/dev/null 2>&1
  elif command -v pacman >/dev/null 2>&1; then pacman -S --needed --noconfirm qemu-guest-agent >/dev/null 2>&1 || echo "pacman failed; if the package databases are stale, run a full upgrade (pacman -Syu) first"
  elif command -v apk >/dev/null 2>&1; then apk add qemu-guest-agent >/dev/null 2>&1
  else echo "No supported package manager found"; exit 3; fi
  command -v qemu-ga >/dev/null 2>&1 || [ -x /usr/sbin/qemu-ga ] || { echo "Installing qemu-guest-agent failed"; exit 1; }
  echo "qemu-guest-agent installed"
fi
if [ -d /run/systemd/system ]; then
  unit=qemu-guest-agent
  systemctl enable "$unit" >/dev/null 2>&1
  systemctl start "$unit" >/dev/null 2>&1
  systemctl is-active "$unit" >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "qemu-guest-agent is not running (the host must expose the virtio channel org.qemu.guest_agent.0)"; exit 1; }
elif command -v rc-service >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  rc-update add qemu-guest-agent default >/dev/null 2>&1
  rc-service qemu-guest-agent start >/dev/null 2>&1
  rc-service qemu-guest-agent status >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "qemu-guest-agent is not running"; exit 1; }
else
  echo "Neither systemd nor OpenRC found"
  exit 3
fi
echo "qemu-guest-agent installed, enabled and running"
exit 0

fields.name: Btrfs device errors check
fields.description: Reads the device error counters of every mounted btrfs filesystem. Exit 1 when any counter is not zero, 3 without btrfs.
fields.script_body:
#!/bin/sh
# Reads the btrfs device error counters of every mounted btrfs filesystem.
# Variables: none
# Exit: 0 all counters zero, 1 errors recorded, 3 btrfs-progs missing or no btrfs filesystem mounted
PATH=/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin
export PATH LC_ALL=C
set -u
command -v awk >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "awk is not installed (install gawk or mawk)"; exit 3; }

grep -q ' btrfs ' /proc/mounts 2>/dev/null || { echo "No btrfs filesystem mounted"; exit 3; }
command -v btrfs >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "Unsupported: btrfs-progs not installed"; exit 3; }
seen='|' bad='' n=0
nl='
'
while read -r dev mp fs _; do
  [ "$fs" = btrfs ] || continue
  case $seen in *"|$dev|"*) continue ;; esac
  seen="$seen$dev|"
  mp=$(printf '%b' "$mp")
  n=$((n + 1))
  out=$(btrfs device stats -- "$mp" 2>&1) || { bad="$bad$mp: cannot read stats: $(printf '%s' "$out" | head -n 1)$nl"; continue; }
  nz=$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | awk '$2 != 0 {print}')
  [ -n "$nz" ] && bad="$bad$(printf '%s\n' "$nz" | sed "s|^|$mp: |")$nl"
done </proc/mounts
if [ -n "$bad" ]; then
  echo "ERROR: btrfs device errors"
  printf '%s' "$bad"
  exit 1
fi
echo "OK: no btrfs device errors ($n filesystems)"

fields.name: Largest directories report
fields.description: Lists the largest first-level directories below a path without crossing into other filesystems. Read only, can take a while on large trees.
fields.script_body:
#!/bin/sh
# Lists the largest first-level directories under PATH, staying on one filesystem.
# Variables: PATH_TO_SCAN (/), TOP (15)
# Exit: 0 report printed, 3 bad input
PATH=/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin
export PATH LC_ALL=C
set -u

P=${PATH_TO_SCAN:-/}
case $P in /*) ;; *) echo "PATH_TO_SCAN must be an absolute path"; exit 3 ;; esac
case $P in *[!A-Za-z0-9/._+@\ -]*) echo "PATH_TO_SCAN has characters that are not allowed"; exit 3 ;; esac
[ -d "$P" ] || { echo "PATH_TO_SCAN is not a directory: $P"; exit 3; }
N=${TOP:-15}
case $N in '' | *[!0-9]*) echo "TOP must be a whole number"; exit 3 ;; esac
{ [ "${#N}" -le 3 ] && [ "$N" -ge 1 ] && [ "$N" -le 200 ]; } || { echo "TOP must be between 1 and 200"; exit 3; }
P=${P%/}

tab=$(printf '\t')
echo "Largest directories under ${P:-/} (one filesystem)"
for e in "$P"/* "$P"/.[!.]* "$P"/..?*; do
  [ -d "$e" ] && [ ! -L "$e" ] || continue
  du -x -k -s "$e" 2>/dev/null
done | sort -rn | head -n "$N" | while IFS="$tab" read -r kb name; do
  if [ "$kb" -ge 1048576 ]; then v=$((kb * 10 / 1048576)); u=G
  elif [ "$kb" -ge 1024 ]; then v=$((kb * 10 / 1024)); u=M
  else v=$((kb * 10)); u=K; fi
  printf '%6s.%s %s  %s\n' "$((v / 10))" "$((v % 10))" "$u" "$name"
done

variables.help: Absolute directory to scan.
variables.name: PATH_TO_SCAN
variables.label: Path

fields.name: Mounts check
fields.description: Checks that mount points are mounted, writable (a test file is created and removed) unless marked :ro, and answer within 10 seconds, which catches hung network mounts. Exit 1 on any problem.
fields.script_body:
#!/bin/sh
# Checks that mount points are mounted, writable (unless marked :ro) and not hung.
# Variables: MOUNTS (one mount point per line, optional :ro suffix for read-only mounts, required)
# Exit: 0 all fine, 1 missing, wrong mode or unresponsive mount, 3 bad input
PATH=/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin
export PATH LC_ALL=C
set -u
command -v awk >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "awk is not installed (install gawk or mawk)"; exit 3; }

LIST=$(printf '%s\n' "${MOUNTS:-}" | tr ',' '\n' | sed 's/^[[:space:]]*//;s/[[:space:]]*$//;/^$/d')
[ -n "$LIST" ] || { echo "MOUNTS is required"; exit 3; }
for m in $LIST; do
  p=${m%:ro}
  case $p in /*) ;; *) echo "Mount point must be an absolute path: $m"; exit 3 ;; esac
  case $p in *[!A-Za-z0-9/._+@-]*) echo "Mount point has characters that are not allowed: $m"; exit 3 ;; esac
done
[ -r /proc/mounts ] || { echo "Unsupported: /proc/mounts not readable"; exit 3; }

probe() {
  ( if [ "$2" = rw ]; then t=$(mktemp "$1/.ulrmm-probe.XXXXXX") && rm -f "$t"; else ls "$1" >/dev/null; fi ) >/dev/null 2>&1 &
  pid=$!
  i=0
  while kill -0 "$pid" 2>/dev/null; do
    i=$((i + 1))
    [ $i -gt 10 ] && return 9
    sleep 1
  done
  wait "$pid"
}

nl='
'
bad='' n=0
for m in $LIST; do
  n=$((n + 1))
  mp=${m%:ro}
  want=rw
  [ "$mp" != "$m" ] && want=ro
  mp=$(printf '%s' "$mp" | sed 's|//*|/|g;s|\(.\)/$|\1|')
  line=$(awk -v m="$mp" '{p = $2; gsub(/\\040/, " ", p); if (p == m) l = $0} END {print l}' /proc/mounts)
  if [ -z "$line" ]; then bad="$bad$mp: not mounted$nl"; continue; fi
  opts=$(printf '%s\n' "$line" | awk '{print $4}')
  fs=$(printf '%s\n' "$line" | awk '{print $3}')
  case ",$opts," in *,ro,*) cur=ro ;; *) cur=rw ;; esac
  if [ "$want" = rw ] && [ "$cur" = ro ]; then bad="$bad$mp: mounted read-only ($fs)$nl"; continue; fi
  if [ "$want" = ro ] && [ "$cur" = rw ]; then bad="$bad$mp: expected read-only but mounted read-write ($fs)$nl"; continue; fi
  probe "$mp" "$want"
  case $? in
  0) ;;
  9) bad="$bad$mp: no answer within 10 seconds, hung mount? ($fs)$nl" ;;
  *) bad="$bad$mp: $([ "$want" = rw ] && echo 'write test failed' || echo 'not readable') ($fs)$nl" ;;
  esac
done
if [ -z "$bad" ]; then
  echo "OK: $n mount points mounted and responding"
  exit 0
fi
echo "ERROR: $(printf '%s' "$bad" | wc -l) of $n mount points have problems"
printf '%s' "$bad"
exit 1

variables.help: Absolute paths, add :ro for read-only mounts. One per line or comma separated.
variables.name: MOUNTS
variables.label: Mount points

fields.name: Software RAID check
fields.description: Reads /proc/mdstat: exit 1 for a degraded array, 2 while a rebuild or check runs, 3 when no md arrays exist.
fields.script_body:
#!/bin/sh
# Checks Linux software RAID (md) arrays for degraded members and running rebuilds.
# Variables: none
# Exit: 0 all arrays healthy, 1 degraded array, 2 rebuild or check running, 3 no md arrays on this system
PATH=/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin
export PATH LC_ALL=C
set -u
command -v awk >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "awk is not installed (install gawk or mawk)"; exit 3; }

[ -r /proc/mdstat ] || { echo "No software RAID: /proc/mdstat not present (md driver not loaded)"; exit 3; }
grep -q '^md' /proc/mdstat || { echo "No software RAID arrays configured"; exit 3; }
res=$(awk '
  /^md/ { name = $1; next }
  /\[[U_]+\]/ { if (match($0, /\[[U_]+\]/)) { s = substr($0, RSTART, RLENGTH); st[name] = s; if (s ~ /_/) bad[name] = 1 } }
  /(resync|recovery|reshape|check) *=/ { act[name] = $0 }
  END { for (n in st) print n, st[n], (n in bad) ? "DEGRADED" : "ok", (n in act) ? "ACTIVITY" : "" }' /proc/mdstat | sort)
n=$(printf '%s\n' "$res" | grep -c .)
if printf '%s\n' "$res" | grep -q DEGRADED; then
  echo "ERROR: degraded RAID array found ($n arrays)"; printf '%s\n' "$res"; exit 1
fi
if printf '%s\n' "$res" | grep -q ACTIVITY; then
  echo "WARNING: RAID rebuild or check running ($n arrays)"; printf '%s\n' "$res"; exit 2
fi
echo "OK: $n RAID arrays healthy"
printf '%s\n' "$res"

fields.name: ZFS pool health check
fields.description: Checks that every imported ZFS pool is ONLINE and shows its fill level. Exit 1 for a degraded or faulted pool, 3 without ZFS.
fields.script_body:
#!/bin/sh
# Checks the health of all ZFS pools.
# Variables: none
# Exit: 0 all pools online, 1 a pool is degraded or faulted, 3 ZFS not installed or no pools
PATH=/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin
export PATH LC_ALL=C
set -u
command -v awk >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "awk is not installed (install gawk or mawk)"; exit 3; }

command -v zpool >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "Unsupported: ZFS tools not installed (zfsutils-linux, zfs or zfs-utils)"; exit 3; }
l=$(zpool list -H -o name,health,capacity 2>&1) || { echo "Cannot query ZFS: $(printf '%s' "$l" | head -n 1)"; exit 3; }
[ -n "$l" ] || { echo "No ZFS pools imported"; exit 3; }
bad=$(printf '%s\n' "$l" | awk -F'\t' '$2 != "ONLINE"')
if [ -n "$bad" ]; then
  echo "ERROR: ZFS pool not online"
  printf '%s\n' "$bad" | awk -F'\t' '{print $1 ": " $2}'
  zpool status -x 2>/dev/null | head -n 20
  exit 1
fi
echo "OK: $(printf '%s\n' "$l" | wc -l) ZFS pools online"
printf '%s\n' "$l" | awk -F'\t' '{print $1 ": " $2 ", " $3 " full"}'

fields.name: Host name
fields.description: Shows the host name, or sets it and updates /etc/hostname and /etc/hosts.
fields.script_body:
#!/bin/sh
# Shows the host name, or sets it (also in /etc/hostname and /etc/hosts).
# Variables: NEW_HOSTNAME (optional, empty = only report).
# Exit codes: 0 done, 1 failed, 3 bad input.
PATH=/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin
export PATH
set -u

command -v awk >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "awk not found: install gawk"; exit 3; }

new=${NEW_HOSTNAME:-}
old=$(hostname 2>/dev/null || cat /proc/sys/kernel/hostname)
if [ -z "$new" ]; then
  echo "Host name: $old"
  exit 0
fi
[ ${#new} -le 253 ] || { echo "NEW_HOSTNAME is longer than 253 characters"; exit 3; }
case $new in -* | .* | *. | *..* | *[!A-Za-z0-9.-]*) echo "NEW_HOSTNAME must be letters, digits, - and . (no leading dash or dot)"; exit 3 ;; esac
oldifs=$IFS
IFS=.
for l in $new; do
  case $l in -* | *-) echo "NEW_HOSTNAME labels must not start or end with a dash"; IFS=$oldifs; exit 3 ;; esac
  [ ${#l} -le 63 ] || { echo "NEW_HOSTNAME label longer than 63 characters"; IFS=$oldifs; exit 3; }
done
IFS=$oldifs
if [ "$old" = "$new" ] && [ "$(cat /etc/hostname 2>/dev/null)" = "$new" ]; then
  echo "Host name already $new"
  exit 0
fi
set_name() {
  if [ -d /run/systemd/system ] && command -v hostnamectl >/dev/null 2>&1 && hostnamectl set-hostname "$new" >/dev/null 2>&1; then return 0; fi
  printf '%s\n' "$new" >/etc/hostname || return 1
  hostname "$new" >/dev/null 2>&1 || printf '%s' "$new" >/proc/sys/kernel/hostname 2>/dev/null
}
set_name || { echo "Setting the host name failed"; exit 1; }
printf '%s\n' "$new" >/etc/hostname 2>/dev/null
if [ -f /etc/hosts ]; then
  tmp=$(mktemp) || exit 1
  short=${new%%.*}
  if grep -Eq '^127\.0\.1\.1[[:space:]]' /etc/hosts; then
    awk -v n="$new" -v s="$short" '/^127\.0\.1\.1[ \t]/ { if (n==s) print "127.0.1.1\t" n; else print "127.0.1.1\t" n " " s; next } {print}' /etc/hosts >"$tmp"
  elif [ "$old" != localhost ] && grep -Eq "(^|[[:space:]])$old([[:space:]]|\$)" /etc/hosts; then
    awk -v o="$old" -v n="$new" '/^#/ {print; next} {for (i=2;i<=NF;i++) if ($i==o) $i=n; print}' /etc/hosts >"$tmp"
  else
    awk '{print}' /etc/hosts >"$tmp"
    printf '127.0.1.1\t%s\n' "$new" >>"$tmp"
  fi
  cat "$tmp" >/etc/hosts
  rm -f "$tmp"
fi
now=$(cat /proc/sys/kernel/hostname)
[ "$now" = "$new" ] || { echo "Host name is $now after the change"; exit 1; }
echo "Host name changed from $old to $new"
if grep -Eqs '^[[:space:]]*manage_etc_hosts:[[:space:]]*(true|template|True)' /etc/cloud/cloud.cfg /etc/cloud/cloud.cfg.d/*.cfg; then
  echo "Note: cloud-init rewrites /etc/hosts at every boot (manage_etc_hosts); change /etc/cloud/templates/hosts.*.tmpl as well"
fi
exit 0
